articles.title: If you want to date ‘Cupertino’ star Ella Stiller, stop making ‘Meet the Parents’ jokes
articles.summary: Ella Stiller has a famous last name, a big TV break and zero interest in AI.
articles.body:
Somehow, up-and-coming actor Ella Stiller keeps finding herself in television projects related to artificial intelligence. In her own life, she doesn't even use AI .

"I've never opened ChatGPT once in my life," she tells Yahoo. "It really upsets me when it has to do with creativity and when it comes into the art world; that's where I get really bummed out."

There are plenty of explorations of that particular technology and more in Cupertino , the new CBS legal drama from the minds of Robert and Michelle King, the creators of The Good Wife . The show centers on a scrappy new law firm in Silicon Valley that takes on David-vs.-Goliath cases against Big Tech. In one storyline, the firm's lawyers have an evolved AI chatbot as a client.

Stiller plays Christy, a plucky jack-of-all-trades and former assistant who gets hired by lawyers Michael Price (Mike Colter) and Olivia Siffre (Rachel Keller) after they were all fired from the same firm. She essentially becomes their investigator, using all her local community relationships to gather evidence that might tip the scales in the case of the week.

If you've watched The Good Wife , Christy is sort of the Kalinda (Archie Panjabi) character, a comparison Stiller doesn't take lightly. Both characters even don combat boots regularly. "It's an honor when people say that — she's the coolest," Stiller says.

Stiller's first acting gig — aside from brief appearances in projects by her father, Ben Stiller, including as a "teen driver" in Escape at Dannemora when she was 16 — came after her graduation from the Juilliard School's prestigious drama program in 2024. The role ended up being connected to one of her favorite TV universes: Sex and the City.

After a summer of auditions, she booked a character seemingly written in the stars on And Just Like That… She played Mia, a salon shampoo girl who becomes pregnant with a child fathered by Miranda's (Cynthia Nixon) son, Brady (Niall Cunningham). In a twist of fate, Brady's fictional grandmother on the show is also her real-life grandmother: four-time Emmy nominee Anne Meara, who died in 2015.

"It was all coincidental," Stiller, whose mother is actor Christine Taylor, says. "I sent in my tape, and they did not know who I was. I felt very connected to her; it was the perfect first job for me."

After a few episodes on And Just Like That… and as Patience in the third season of The Comeback (another show that tackles AI), Stiller is sinking her teeth into a 20-episode season of television. It's a return to full-episode orders that makes for satisfying character arcs, a rarity in today's television landscape.

Stiller, who still tunes in to Grey's Anatomy , equates turning on the TV to watch a long-running series as "hanging out with a group of friends." Cupertino is set to air until spring 2027, giving viewers lots to chew on. At just 24, Stiller seems poised for a promising career ahead.

In our latest Generation Now interview, Stiller discusses the giggly energy on the set of Cupertino , her foray into astrology and what it's like to bring a partner home to meet the family.

How would you describe your experience working on 'Cupertino' and with showrunners Robert and Michelle King?

It's been an absolute dream. They're such incredible leaders. They're so smart and their energy is so positive and they love this show so much. I ended up working with the greatest television showrunners ever.

You seem to be picking very smart projects.

And very AI-conscious projects! In this industry and with this job, there's so much heartbreak and rejection. The second that you find people that you gel with and that get you, that see you and want to work with you, and that you want to work with … that's been my experience, with The Comeback and with this, a real seeing of each other.

Any favorite memories so far working with Mike Colter and Rachel Keller?

I love them so much. We laugh a lot. Maybe it's cliché, but we do. There was a day where me, Mike and Busy Philipps were in some weird mansion in New Jersey. That was a day of delirium and the giggles coming out, right in the halfway point where it was like, are we going insane? It's always fun when we get to go to the weird locations because we all bond over the fact that this place is weird, right? Sometimes it's beautiful, but sometimes you're in a weird basement waiting to shoot, and you don't know who's been there.

OK, I've gotten really interested in astrology. So I've been doing a lot of investigating on that front. I've been listening to a lot of podcasts and doing a lot of research on what is happening every week, astrologically. What are the planets doing? A lot of people experienced a weird summer because this was a really crazy summer astrologically. I've become the person people ask: Like, wait, is something happening this week that I should know about? And I'm like, yeah, Venus is in retrograde.

You're an Aries. Do you think Christy is also an Aries?

I do. I totally think she is. I always want to be able to think of something else so that it's a little bit separate from me, but I just think she's totally an Aries. I don't think it's a question. I'm an Aries with a Pisces moon, so I cry a lot. I'm very sensitive. I haven't investigated this properly enough, but I have a sneaking suspicion that most actors have a water sign moon for being sensitive and open and feeling. I think as an actor, it's all about letting the world and every single interaction you have affect you, hit your emotions and your heart, and make you cry or make you laugh. That's what a water sign moon does. That's my theory.

I don't use AI. It just wasn't of use to me when it was first coming out, and people didn't know how dangerous it was or the environmental implications. I was in drama school, I wasn't writing papers, so that was never going to be of any use to me. I believe so deeply that art is humanity. So I hate the idea that AI could affect that, but I also have a lot of hope and a major trust that people aren't going to buy it. No one's going to be into AI writing and AI actors.

Do you think 20-episode TV seasons are finally back?

I really hope! They don't really do it anymore, but we get to do it. It's so exciting. We finish shooting the season on Friday, and I'm getting separation anxiety. But we're then gonna be on the air for the next 16 weeks or something; that keeps it alive even in our off time. How great to get to dive in that way as an actor. But also as a viewer, you get such a sense of the world; you get a deep dive and the luxury of having all of this time to let it all play out. It's a treat for everyone.

You're canonically in the 'Sex and the City' universe as the mother of your real-life grandmother's TV character's great-grandchild. Did I get that right?

So I am Brady's baby mama, and Brady's grandma is my grandma. That's the real meta version of it. Canonically, Mia has no relation to Steve's mom. But yeah, it's trippy. That was my first TV gig out of school. I graduated in May 2024. I auditioned all summer, and at the end of the summer got this amazing guest star role. I saw [that] it was And Just Like That… and I was like, I have to do it. I love Sex and the City . There are very few auditions as an actor where you immediately feel it's a match made in heaven. It really felt meant to be because I felt like [my grandmother] was up there watching over me. I love that … I play the girl who's carrying Miranda's grandchild. Miranda's the best.

I can't help but think of 'Focker-in-Law.' What has it been like to bring someone home to meet your dad?

Listen. My dating history, whatever, but never have they passed up the opportunity to make that [ Meet the Parents ] joke. And it's always real funny. I find it real funny — not at all. It's not my favorite joke, but I get it. I hold space for it because I understand. I understand that it's maybe an obligatory joke. It's a joke that constantly gets made, and I'm like, you're brilliant, aren't you? "Never heard that one before," that's what I always say. And honestly, I'm very particular about who I introduce to my family and stuff. When it has happened a couple times, it's real rich.

New episodes of Cupertino air every Thursday at 10 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+ .

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

articles.summary: Kim Kardashian's White House meetings, Kanye West coparenting struggles and Kris Jenner's affair are explored in "Citizen Kim" by Jonathan Van Meter.
articles.body: Kim Kardashian's life is explored in a new book chronicling her meteoric rise to fame. In the new book, "Citizen Kim: The Woman Who Created the Future," writer Jonathan Van Meter dove deep into the lives of the Kardashians, particularly Kim, and how she built her empire outside of reality TV. Through a series of interviews with members of the Kardashian family, including Kim, Khloe and Kourtney, as well as those close to the famous family, Van Meter discusses the biggest moments in her life, including her relationship with Kanye, the terrifying Paris robbery, her mother's affair and her prison reform and advocacy work. White House warnings In October 2017, Kim saw a video of Alice Marie Johnson in prison, in which she was pleading for clemency. She opened up in the book about how the video "changed my life," saying she immediately reached out to Shawn Holley, who was a lawyer on O.J. Simpson's defense team, asking "What can we do?" After learning the only way to get Johnson out of prison was a presidential pardon, Kim reached out to Ivanka Trump, who put her in touch with Jared Kushner. Kushner helped set up a meeting between Kardashian and President Trump, a move that raised concerns on both sides about the "optics," according to the book. "Everyone was telling me, ‘Don’t go, your career will be over; you can’t step foot in there.’ And I was like, ‘It’s my reputation over someone’s life?’ Weigh that out," Kim said in the book. "People talk s--- about me all day long. It will just be another story about me versus someone getting their life back." A week after the meeting with President Trump, Kim was able to call Johnson and personally deliver the news that she had been granted clemency. "She started screaming on the phone. I was on the set of a Steven Klein shoot, practically nude, so I had to cover with a robe and make this call and tell her," Kim said. "She packed her stuff—whatever she checked in with twenty two years prior—and was released immediately." Oval Office meeting Kim's experience advocating on behalf of Johnson was her first step on the path towards becoming a lawyer and furthering her advocacy work. She met with President Trump again, this time on behalf of a man who received a life sentence for a nonviolent crime. This time, she was accompanied by attorney Van Jones, who said he will "never forget walking into the West Wing with her." While Jones felt as if "Every sentence I said made it worse," he recalled Kim and the president discussing the case, including Kardashian's response after Trump said, "This guy . . . let's just be honest now. This is a tough guy." "Kim had memorized the case," Jones said in the book. "She knew everything about the person. She told the president, ‘You can be the big guy; you can help a sick man.’ It was like watching a ballerina hypnotize a grizzly bear . . . her syllable-to-impact ratio is off the charts. What she can get done in a simple sentence!" Jones argued in the book that while some may resent Kim because "she represents somebody who already has it all" and is now trying to also "be successful in my field," he says, "if you’re in jail, and you’re trying to get out, you’re not mad at Kim Kardashian." KIM KARDASHIAN WOWS IN STRING BIKINI DURING PDA-FILLED BEACH TRIP WITH LEWIS HAMILTON "You have literally hundreds of thousands of people for whom the system is so broken that only when a Kim Kardashian steps in does she change the odds in their favor, even a little bit," he said. "So you can be mad at Kim or you can be mad at the system that is so broken that it needs Kim." Kanye concerns Kim married rapper Kanye West in May 2014 and welcomed four children together before filing for divorce in February 2021. Towards the end of their marriage, West began acting increasingly erratic as he dealt with ongoing mental health issues and began speaking negatively about Kim and her family members. Kim expressed in the past that this led her to not feel safe around him, emotionally and physically. That’s the father of my kids, I’ll never not worry about him. And that’s a big burden of having kids with someone who you don’t necessarily get along with. My kids would never know that. I do everything in my power to forget about all the negative things that happened," she said. "I have to be realistic, and my therapist definitely tells me, ‘Your boundaries have to go up,’ but we manage to coparent without too much conflict. It’s been pretty smooth for while. I guess because we don’t talk that much. But when we see each other, we give each other a hug." She added that she not only encourages her children to have a relationship with their father, but also with his family, noting that whenever his family members are in town, she will invite them over for dinner and to spend time with her kids. Although he was acting erratic in public, Kim noted their children never saw him that way, adding, "That was such a blessing." Or: Is it go-time?" she said. "My whole household knows what a ‘lockdown’ means if I text it. Like, ‘We’re on lockdown.’ No TVs, just movies. No just plug in a phone for music in the car. articles.title: Inside Saif Ali Khan's Rs 800 crore Pataudi Palace which has 150 rooms, grand verandas, Venetian chandeliers and more
articles.summary: Saif Ali Khan's ancestral property, the Pataudi Palace, is spread across 10 acres and is located around 30 kilometres from Gurugram.
articles.body: Saif Ali Khan's ancestral property, the Pataudi Palace, is spread across 10 acres and is located around 30 kilometres from Gurugram. Built in 1935, the grand residence was commissioned by the last ruling Nawab of Pataudi, Iftikhar Ali Khan, for his wife. According to reports, the property was leased to the Neemrana Hotels group in 2005. Saif later reclaimed ownership of the palace for a reported Rs 800 crore following the death of his father, Nawab Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi.According to Architectural Digest, the sprawling property has nearly 150 rooms, including seven bedrooms, seven dressing rooms, seven billiard rooms, along with expansive dining and drawing rooms.The palace's architecture was designed by Robert Tor Russell, who gave the property a distinctive European neoclassical influence through clean lines and geometric patterns. While the interiors retain elements of Indian heritage through traditional floral motifs, framed photographs of the Pataudi royal family lend a personal touch to the space.The palace's long corridors reportedly feature striking black-and-white chequered marble flooring, while the walls are painted in understated shades of yellow, white, cream and pastel colours. Another highlight is its vintage library, which recently caught attention after Saif shared a glimpse of it in one of his Instagram posts.The dining area reportedly features crystal chandeliers, decorative lamps, elegant vases and warm lighting. Potted plants placed across different corners add a touch of greenery to the interiors. The bedrooms, meanwhile, combine wooden flooring, ornate heritage details, antique decor and handcrafted furniture.Among the palace's most distinctive architectural features is a dome inspired by the Sanchi Stupa, supported by imposing columned pillars. High-ceilinged verandas, parquet flooring and pink Venetian chandeliers further add to the regal character of the property, making Pataudi Palace a striking blend of Indian heritage and European architectural influences.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Cynthia Erivo reacts to criticism over her close friendship with Ariana Grande: ‘Two women could actually be friends’
articles.summary: Actor Cynthia Erivo has responded to criticism surrounding her close friendship with 'Wicked' co-star Ariana Grande, saying there appeared to be an
articles.body: Actor Cynthia Erivo has responded to criticism surrounding her close friendship with 'Wicked' co-star Ariana Grande, saying there appeared to be an unusual level of annoyance among fans at the idea of two women sharing a genuine bond, according to People.In an interview, Erivo spoke about the reactions to the actresses' off-screen friendship during the promotional tours of 'Wicked' and its sequel 'Wicked: For Good'."It was interesting that there were many people who had become psychologists from their couches," Erivo said. "There was this weird sort of, what’s the word I’m looking for … annoyance … at the fact that two women could actually be friends,” as per the outlet.Erivo said some fans appeared to question the authenticity of the emotions the two actresses displayed during interviews and promotional events, including their expressions of affection, laughter and tears."Like, ‘Why are they friends? Why are they connected? There must be something wrong with them. Why are they showing emotion? How dare they cry? And how dare they laugh? And how dare they be emotive and alive?’ " she said.Describing the reaction as a "double-edged sword", Erivo said the actresses would likely have faced criticism even if they had displayed little emotion during their public appearances."Because if we were dead behind the eyes and showing no emotion, there would have been something else to say about it," she said, adding that she wished someone could have shown them the "proper balance" of emotion to express.Erivo also recalled the November 13, 2025 incident in Singapore, when she stepped in to shield Grande after a fan ran towards the singer and put his arm around her during a promotional event.Describing the incident as "terrifying", Erivo said her immediate reaction was to protect her co-star."No one else was moving. We were on a carpet," she said. "We were exposed. My immediate response was: ‘Get this man away from us now,’” according to People.She also objected to the suggestion that she was acting as Grande's "bodyguard", saying her response was simply that of a friend looking out for another friend."I was like: ‘Oh, you think because I look like this that you could talk to me this way about something that was a human thing that I would have done for any friend, and hopefully a friend would have done for me,’" she said.Erivo and Grande played Elphaba and Glinda, respectively, in the two-part musical adaptation of the Tony-winning Broadway production. The films, released in 2024 and 2025, follow the friendship between the two characters, who meet as college roommates at the fictional Shiz University and gradually discover their identities.The actresses' friendship also drew appreciation from the film's collaborators. Director Jon M. Chu had previously described their bond as "one of the most beautiful friendships to watch grow" in an interview with People."These two are the two biggest voices in the world, maybe in our lifetime. They could have hated each other," Chu said, adding that despite the possibility of "insane divaship", the actresses consistently placed the film ahead of themselves and immersed themselves in their respective characters.The two actresses have continued to share a close bond following the films' releases. In November 2025, they also revealed that they had got matching "For Good" tattoos inked on their palms.Meanwhile, Erivo recently starred in 'Prima Facie', a legal drama that premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September. articles.title: Chrishell Stause’s G Flip Split Gets Messier As Insider Reveals Alleged Fights
articles.summary: Chrishell Stause and G Flip presented a relationship that seemed to have everything: public declarations of love, matching tattoos, extravagant […]
articles.body:
Chrishell Stause and G Flip presented a relationship that seemed to have everything: public declarations of love, matching tattoos, extravagant trips and plans to build a family.

Their romance even appeared to survive the pressures of a demanding entertainment career. However, the picture painted by an insider following their separation was considerably less idyllic, with claims that frequent arguments, competing priorities and growing tension had been wearing down the marriage-like partnership long before the couple announced their breakup.

Chrishell Stause's Career Transition Allegedly Put Pressure On Their Relationship

One of the biggest sources of tension reportedly emerged when Chrishell Stause left "Selling Sunset" after nine seasons.

According to the Daily Mail 's insider, the reality star struggled with what came next professionally and wanted another major television opportunity that never materialized.

"She is very ambitious. She wanted to be on a big reality TV show after Selling Sunset, she felt she deserved that, but it didn't materialize because Hollywood is tricky," the source claimed.

The insider suggested that Stause's desire to remain visible in the entertainment industry began affecting her relationship with G Flip.

According to the source, she became increasingly focused on maintaining her celebrity image, attending events and securing the kind of treatment associated with a major star.

"She needed the private car, stylist, red carpet, great photos, gift bag, she fell into the trap. She loved staying in the news," the insider added.

An eyewitness also described Stause's behavior at a Beverly Hills rooftop party hosted by Snapchat, claiming she arrived with a large entourage and appeared difficult to approach. The witness said she had "big movie star energy."

The insider further alleged that G Flip became frustrated with the attention Stause expected, claiming she wanted their partner's time and attention largely to herself. "But G Flip has their own career," the source pointed out.

Stause And G Flip's Alleged Arguments Took An Emotional Toll

The reported disagreements were not simply about professional ambitions. The insider claimed that the couple had been fighting frequently for more than a year, with the tension eventually exhausting G Flip.

"They began fighting a lot and it really wore G Flip out. G Flip didn't like the drama," the source alleged.

They also suggested that their different stages of life contributed to the difficulties. Christel Stause is 45, while G Flip is 33.

Although the source acknowledged that the age difference did not take away from Stause's appearance, they suggested it could have created insecurities.

The couple's public romance had initially appeared effortless. They met at a Halloween party in Los Angeles while both were dressed as skeletons, and the insider described their immediate connection as unusually intense.

"They had incredible chemistry right away, which took them both aback," the source recalled.

Their relationship moved quickly, with declarations of love, luxury holidays and public appearances becoming part of their story. They eventually held a non-legally binding wedding ceremony in Las Vegas in 2023 and later renewed their vows in July 2025.

Chrishell Stause's Family Plans Added Another Layer To Their Separation

The couple's separation also marked the end of a relationship that had included serious conversations about having children.

Stause had previously explained that differing views on starting a family contributed to her breakup with "Selling Sunset" co-star Jason Oppenheim.

With G Flip, however, she appeared to have found someone who shared her desire to become a parent.

In April 2025, Stause said she was "actively trying" to grow their family, while G Flip spoke openly about the emotional difficulty of undergoing in vitro fertilization.

In September 2025, the musician described the IVF process to PEOPLE as "really sad" and "very grim."

Chrishell Stause's former "Selling Sunset" co-stars reportedly questioned her behavior during her relationship with G Flip, with Bre Tiesi weighing in on the split.

G Flip previously admitted that appearing on "Selling Sunset" made them uncomfortable , despite their relationship with Stause.

Stause's departure from "Selling Sunset" reportedly left producers scrambling to find a celebrity replacement following her nine-season run.

Chrishell Stause's feud with Nicole Young escalated after the reality star threatened to leave the Netflix series.

Before their separation, Stause revealed that she leaned heavily on G Flip to navigate the emotional pressures of filming "Selling Sunset."

G Flip's former relationship with Stause attracted attention after Jason Oppenheim reacted to their wedding following his own breakup with the reality star.

Stause Was Reportedly Blindsided When G Flip's Feelings Changed

The circumstances surrounding Chrishell Stause and G Flip's separation took a different turn when a report suggested the breakup was not driven by the frequent arguments and personality clashes previously alleged by an insider.

According to TMZ , G Flip had fallen out of love with Stause romantically, leaving the reality television star heartbroken and reportedly unprepared for the decision.

Sources close to the former couple revealed that G Flip had begun viewing Stause more as a friend than a romantic partner.

The Australian musician reportedly travelled from Australia to Los Angeles to have a difficult conversation with Stause about the change in their feelings.

The report also challenged the suggestion that Stause's alleged demanding behavior or reputation for being difficult had caused the relationship to collapse.

Instead, the sources described their time together as a good relationship that had reached a painful turning point because G Flip's romantic feelings had changed.

Chrishell Stause's Long-Distance Relationship With G Flip Faced An Unavoidable Strain

Questions about who ended the relationship were accompanied by another explanation for why the couple struggled to maintain it.

PEOPLE reported that G Flip had initiated the separation after more than four years together, while an insider identified the distance between them as a major factor.

"The distance is what really drove the two of them apart," the source told the publication. The insider explained that their demanding travel arrangements had made sustaining the relationship increasingly difficult, particularly as they lived on opposite sides of the world.

"They were trying to make the 'marriage,' that was never legal, work. They both wanted to have kids, but they also both didn't want to uproot their lives for the other," the source said. The insider added that the long flights, weeks apart and time difference had taken their toll.

The report also revealed that the possibility of reconciliation had not been completely ruled out. According to the source, both Stause and G Flip still had strong feelings for each other, despite the decision to separate.

"Chrishell and G Flip still very much love each other and haven't ruled anything out, as far as reuniting romantically, in the future," the insider explained.

articles.title: New movies to watch this weekend: See 'The Mongoose' and 'Everest: The Other Side' in theaters, rent or buy 'Verity,' stream 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' on Prime Video
articles.summary: "The Mongoose" is a Liam Neeson vehicle about Liam Neeson in a vehicle. But I was wowed by one chilling new release.
articles.body:
Welcome to Trust Me, I Watch Everything , a weekly guide to notable new movies opening or becoming available each Friday.

It's a fairly slow week in theaters. Instead of some buzzy wide releases, we're getting a handful of smaller films, including Liam Neeson's The Mongoose and the IMAX-sized documentary Everest: The Other Side.

If you'd prefer a movie night at home, you can rent or buy the latest Colleen Hoover adaptation Verity with Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson, or check out Ridley Scott's post-apocalyptic drama The Dog Stars starring Jacob Elordi and Josh Brolin.

Over on streaming services you're likely already paying for, Ali G: Who Iz I? makes its way from theaters to Prime Video, and Minions & Monsters is finally on Peacock.

Last but not least, it's Halloween weekend! I've rounded up 37 of my horror faves — some satisfyingly spooky, some truly sick — for those planning an at-home fright fest.

Why you should skip it: I've been known to enjoy my fair share of late-period Liam Neeson actioners, but this one is a real low-rent snoozefest.

Neeson plays a falsely accused war hero with nothing to lose as he leads police on an epic televised cross-country car chase. He's helped by members of his former Special Forces Army battalion (including Ving Rhames), and closely monitored by a fascinated public rooting for his safe getaway. Marisa Tomei stars as his ex-wife, and Michael Chiklis is the lead cop on his tail.

The problem isn't the performances — everybody is serviceable-to-good here — but the editing, clunky pacing and amateurish directing from first-time filmmaker (and Neeson's longtime stunt coordinator) Mark Vanselow. There are a lot of flashbacks and attempts to tie Neeson's PTSD into his current predicament.

It eventually becomes a story about people across the country watching the car chase on TV and learning about this guy's story, earning him grassroots support as the police chase him for a crime we'll learn about over the course of the film. This is the most interesting element of the movie, but it feels like it comes too late.

The movie is mostly Liam Neeson behind the wheel of a car, and while the use of real vehicles is worth praising, that's where the compliments begin and end. The stunt driving has its moments, but there aren't enough of them to recommend watching this.

As such, it's for Neeson completionists only.

What other critics are saying : They're not kind. Mark Dujsik of Mark Reviews Movies writes, "The makers of this chase movie clearly are more interested in the variety of vehicles they can play with than in any of the human characters in this story." Robert Kojder of Flickering Myth adds, "This isn't saying much given the track record of the past 10 years or so of Liam Neeson's filmography, but this is especially dull and dreadful even for his recent roles."

How to watch: The Mongoose is now playing in theaters nationwide .

Why you should skip it: This allegedly inspirational documentary is described as an intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition and the pursuit of the impossible. Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell deeply in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski the direct north face of Mount Everest, the most difficult and dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on Earth. It's something only a handful have ever achieved, and no one has successfully skied down.

Maybe becoming a parent has softened me, but I found this movie borderline despicable. It treats a dangerous and stupid vanity project like skiing down Everest as if it were some important mission this couple simply had to do rather than a dumb thing no one should ever do, especially as parents with young kids. It's as if everybody is shocked when an avalanche occurs at the avalanche factory!

I just can't imagine finding this inspiring or anything but a horror show about people stuck in cycles of tragedy, and then engaging in more tragedy to make it mean something. I found it difficult to laud their efforts as an example of drive and persistence rather than, say, recklessness. What is presented as a tribute struck me as bone-chilling in retrospect, and the film feels overly reverent rather than digging into anything thorny. Cool shots of the mountains, though!

What other critics are saying : I'm in the minority on this one. AP's Jake Coyle says the movie "becomes a mournful and increasingly solitary march." I'm more with Variety's Guy Lodge , who writes, "To Morrison, as well as to the filmmakers, this awful backstory makes something cathartic of his accomplishment. Many in the audience, however, will query the point of it all."

How to watch: Everest: The Other Side is now playing in theaters nationwide .

Breeder : An ingenious premise and a terrific lead performance really make Breeder stand out from similar low-budget indie horror fare. An eccentric poodle breeder (Dot-Marie Jones) lures a broke college student to her remote ranch with a promise of research funding. He soon learns that there's a catch. The twist is best discovered in real time, so let's just say this woman is actually interested in breeding more than just animals. Get tickets .

My colleague Kelsey Weekman covered this one.

Why you should probably skip it: We can't talk about Verity the movie without first talking about Verity the book.

It's a novel by Colleen Hoover, the modern queen of WTF-romance who's also responsible for It Ends with Us. I really can't overstate her impact: She outsold the Bible in 2022 and built a pop-star-level fan army to become one of the few living authors considered a household name. Hoover's books, which are wildly popular on the bookish side of the internet, are soapy, emotional and — let's be honest — pretty bad. But that's what makes them delicious. And Verity is the most delicious of them all. It's a one-star book that offers a five-star reading experience.

In the film, Dakota Johnson plays a struggling novelist named Lowen who's hired to take over a popular series as a ghostwriter after its original author, Verity (Anne Hathaway), is incapacitated. Lowen moves into Verity's home, becomes entangled with Verity's husband Jeremy (Josh Hartnett) and uncovers Verity's disturbing autobiographical writing that may be evidence of a crime.

I found myself begging the cinematic gods that the movie version of Verity would feel just as ridiculous as the book. It's an erotic thriller that's heavy on bonkers plot points. For instance, it opens with Lowen witnessing a car crash and getting blood spattered all over her clothes right before an important meeting. Later, she bites her headboard at the exact same place Verity once left bite marks. No spoilers, but Verity is portrayed as so ghoulishly cruel toward her children that she might as well be a cartoon witch.

The movie preserves many of the book's wilder happenings, but Hoover's quirkily absurd writing style is extracted from the screen, which sucks the campiness right out of it. It's not bad enough to be good in a fun way, but it's also not good enough to be authentically good. Hathaway, in her fifth movie of the year , seems to be having the most fun. And I appreciated that it's likely the first movie to feature a Hot Ones interview as a major plot point.

I once gleefully watched videos about the book titled " Verity by Colleen Hoover is an unhinged dumpster fire. And that's an understatement." and " Verity by Colleen Hoover is literally the WORST book ever written". But I could never summon that much emotion to talk about the movie, which is ultimately just fine.

What other critics are saying: The ones who like it find it fun and campy , but the ones who don't went hard. "A flat-footed dud, at once overwrought and underplotted, and barely propped up by A-list stars who look either embarrassed, confused or indifferent to be there," Variety's Guy Lodge writes . TheWrap's Amelia Emberwing says Verity has its issues, but it "feels like the perfect movie to put on with your girlfriends."

How to watch: Verity is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV , Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Why you should skip it: Ridley Scott's post-apocalyptic "thriller" — I put that in quotes for a reason — is not the action-heavy sci-fi flick that the trailers are selling. To put it simply, The Dog Stars is a shockingly derivative work that audiences have seen before, and there's just not enough variation or anything unique done with the subject matter here to recommend it.

Based on the 2012 book of the same name , The Dog Stars is set in a world ravaged by a pandemic. A widowed man (a brooding Jacob Elordi) lives a lonesome existence in a Colorado airplane hangar with his dog and a dour gunman he has befriended (Josh Brolin). When a mysterious transmission comes over the radio while he's flying his old Cessna, it sparks a hunt for its source.

It's every bit as generic as that sounds, and there unfortunately aren't any real surprises along the way. Despite admirable work from the cast, it never fully grabs you. It's so dull that I found my mind wandering to the question of why anybody would make this particular movie in 2026. There are obvious COVID parallels, but the film doesn't do anything with them. It feels dated and so familiar that it constantly begs the question: why?!

The biggest problem with it is that it lacks propulsiveness, or any sort of energy, really, until it's far too late. There's some action and excitement in the third act, which is well-staged in typical Ridley Scott fashion, though it feels at odds with the more grounded, melancholic, character-focused drama that makes up the rest of the film. The script is the biggest issue here, as the characters come off as archetypes more than real people. Scott is a strong enough director that his contributions, including some stunning aerial photography, do impress even when the rest is boring you to tears.

The Dog Stars does come to life at a certain point toward the end of its punishing 2-hour runtime — an uncanny sequence with Allison Janney has more verve than the rest of them combined — but the rest is as forgettable as movies get.

What other critics are saying : It's getting brutal reviews. TheWrap's William Bibbiani writes, "There are way too many faults in these Stars . Woof." Monica Castillo at the AV Club adds, "This messy look at the end of the world isn't Scott's darkest film, but it's one of his worst misfires."

How to watch: The Dog Stars is now available to rent or buy on Apple TV, Prime Video and other VOD platforms.

Ghost in the Cell : Indonesian genre filmmaker Joko Anwar ( Satan's Slaves, Impetigore) returns with a horror movie that leans more toward comedy, unafraid of going too silly and over-the-top. At a notorious prison, an invisible force begins killing inmates brutally, compelling enemy gangs and corrupt guards to work together as they try to survive the mounting bloodshed. It's probably the closest we'll ever come to an extremely R-rated Stephen Chow horror movie. The wackiness of Chow is there, but it's all filtered through insane gore and staged death scenes that feel straight out of the beloved Hannibal TV series. It's an ambitious soup that also functions as biting social commentary on government corruption, and there's even a plot-driven reason why these characters must dance. You've truly never seen anything quite like this one. Rent or buy .

Never After Dark : Fans of Japanese horror movies are in for a treat, as Never After Dark plays like an arthouse take on something like The Grudge . A traveling psychic who helps lost souls cross over encounters a powerful entity at a remote house. While investigating its origins, she uncovers dark secrets and faces a deadly threat from an unexpected source. The movie's approach to the spooky stuff is terrific — it really nails the balance between the supernatural and staying firmly grounded in reality. The main character is assisted by her sister, who died when they were young and is now forever a teenager in the spirit realm. It's just a really good ghost story, told with both care and gusto, and positively dripping with atmosphere. Mainstream American horror movies like The Conjuring and its sequels should aspire to be this good and tense. Rent or buy .

Forgotten Island : This new original animated movie from DreamWorks is beautifully designed and equally beautiful in its messaging about nostalgia and how you'll always have the memories of the ones you loved, no matter how far you drift apart in life. The movie itself is extremely busy and frenetic, jumping from one otherworldly character introduction to another as our leads traverse the titular forgotten island to which they've been magically transported. But it's laugh-out-loud funny throughout, and the bond between the two leads is so palpable that it all works in spite of its nonstop raucous energy. DreamWorks Animation is often thought of as "less than" Pixar; this movie feels like an attempt to hit the emotional highs that that studio is known for, and it works quite well. It's charming and sweet, and the characters learn important, bittersweet life lessons along the way. Rent or buy .

Why you should skip it: Ali G: Who Iz I? sees Sacha Baron Cohen return to a comedic character best left in the past, and that idea of his irrelevance in the modern era is the entire engine of the movie. Unfortunately, it lacks the laugh-out-loud antics of Borat , even though it does manage to deliver some of the same "holy crap" moments associated with Baron Cohen's 2018 Showtime satire series Who Is America?

After 20 years spent "chillin', tokin' and bonin'", Ali G (Baron Cohen) is surprised to discover that his long-term girlfriend, Julie, is eight months pregnant. Faced with an extra mouth to feed, he heads to America to reclaim his former glory, but soon encounters adversaries who will ultimately threaten his and his child's very existence.

In addition to Ali G, Baron Cohen also plays a couple of other characters, including Who Is America?' s Col. Erran Morad, a former Mossad agent, as well as the ultra-woke leftie Dr. Nira Cain-N'Degeocello, who becomes the butt of jokes about cultural appropriation.

It all comes off a bit stale and largely lacks the shocking "people reveal unflattering things about themselves" energy that makes Borat and even Bruno occasionally insightful. There is a section, however, that features Baron Cohen tricking a bunch of right-wing provocateurs into thinking they're committing crimes, and that bit feels more in line with what Who Is America? was all about.

Too much of the humor relies on a Baron Cohen character waltzing into a room and acting insane as the camera pans around to capture unsuspecting people's reactions. Saying provocative things in a room full of people who are not going to take kindly to it just feels cheap and lazy here, and the reactions aren't particularly compelling.

Ali G: Who Iz I? feels like it's trying to make the point that both sides of the political aisle are so extreme nowadays that everybody deserves to be made fun of equally. But that thesis doesn't exactly hold up even within the movie itself.

What other critics are saying : Most are negative, but there are some fans, like Nick Schager at the Daily Beast , who writes, "Despite its inherent limitations and more than a handful of easy-target gags, it's always mildly amusing — and, on a couple of memorable occasions, legitimately laugh-out-loud funny." TheWrap's Todd Gilchrist , however, writes, "Whether he's considered repugnant or delightful, Sacha Baron Cohen has always elicited a strong reaction. Ali G: Who Iz I? does not. After a quarter of a century pushing boundaries, that makes this his most offensive project yet."

How to watch: Ali G: Who Iz I? is now streaming on Prime Video .

Why you should watch it: This $5 billion franchise for children didn't have to make a feature-length love letter to making movies that's as full of references from the silent era and the Golden Age of Hollywood as it is to more modern allusions like Spielberg movies and a literal George Lucas cameo, but I'm glad they did. The nods to George Méliès, Citizen Kane, Metropolis and the antics of Buster Keaton and Harold Lloyd may be lost on your toddlers, but film critics, and hopefully parents at large, should appreciate them. The Minions are now the kings of Hollywood, and they're paying their respects.

Minions & Monsters, the third standalone Minions film, but seventh overall in the Despicable Me universe, tells the story of how the Minions conquered Hollywood, became movie stars, lost everything, unleashed monsters onto the world and then banded together to try to save the planet from the mayhem they had just created. It's Babylon for babies; those yellow guys are Singin' in the Rain !

As someone mostly aware of the Minions through pop culture osmosis rather than actually watching the previous films, I still found most of the jokes that involve shoving these creatures into cinema history to be clever, funny and kind of impressive. They work as slapstick for children, but have more value to the cinephile parents whose kids dragged them to the theater.

When the movie shifts gears to focus on the actual plot and the titular monsters that were promised, it's less engaging and more slapdash, but I doubt the intended audience of children will mind. There are a couple of off-color jokes that arguably go too far, including a beheading gag that was maybe a bit much for a movie that I took my 3-year-old to, but it's more confusing than upsetting. There are so many subplots that the throughline is hard to find, but those sequences serve a dual purpose in referencing the types of movies being paid homage to here.

As a former cinema studies major, Minions & Monsters played to my specific interests, and I appreciated that my kid and I could both have fun watching it. Since these movies inherently owe a debt to silent-era comedy, making that connection explicit within the film itself is meaningful and may even inspire kids to seek out the classics; nobody tell them the Minions don't appear! Between Minions & Monsters and Jackass: Best and Last , the legacy of Buster Keaton is alive and well.

What other critics are saying: Appealing to the film dorks paid off, as it's the best-reviewed entry in the series. Amy Nicholson of the Los Angeles Times writes, "I'll admit, I snorted the first time I saw a TikTok of teens gussied up in suits to see a Minions movie. But after watching Minions & Monsters make nods to Metropolis and Casablanca , I understand." Adds Damon Wise at Deadline : "The whole thing is an anarchic delirium reminiscent of the kind experienced by Bart and Milhouse after drinking an all-syrup Super Squishee; thankfully, the comedown is quick and relatively painless."

How to watch: Minions & Monsters is now streaming on Peacock .

Gentle Monster : Lea Seydoux is extraordinary in this disturbing drama about a woman discovering that her husband, the father of her child, is charged with possession of child sexual abuse material. Filmmaker Marie Kreutzer expands the scope of the film as we follow the female police officer assigned to the case and see the troubles she herself is having with her aging father. The film seems to suggest that there's no such thing as a "good man" and that monstrous, evil behavior can lurk in both the most unexpected places and the most normal-seeming people. It reminded me a bit of You Can See Everything, the movie of the moment, in that it's ultimately about the unknowability of others. It's an unsettling and uncomfortable viewing experience. Now streaming on Netflix.

That's all for this week! We'll see you next Friday.

articles.title: 'Game of Thrones' actor Nikolaj Coster-Waldau spends night in Kyiv Metro amid Russian air raid threat
articles.summary: Danish actor Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, best known for playing Jaime Lannister in Game of Thrones, took shelter alongside Ukrainian residents in aKyiv
articles.body: Danish actor Nikolaj Coster-Waldau, best known for playing Jaime Lannister in Game of Thrones, took shelter alongside Ukrainian residents in aKyiv metrostation during aRussian air raidthreat.'Game of Thrones' actor Nikolaj Coster-Waldau spent a night in a metro station in Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv, as residents sought shelter amid aRussian air raidthreat.The Danish actor, who serves as a Goodwill Ambassador for the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), shared details of the experience on his Instagram Stories.He was in Kyiv as part of efforts to raise awareness about the situation in Ukraine amid the ongoing war.“Spent a night in the Kyiv Metro. Pretty rough night. I get to do it one night and tell the tale but for thousands of Ukrainians it's a necessity to be safe during the shelling. We need to keep helping the civilians and uphold the rules we all agree on,” he wrote.Photographs obtained by Page Six showed Coster-Waldau resting on a cot inside the metro station. He was seen wearing a blue UNDP hoodie, khaki cargo pants and black sneakers. Other pictures showed him inside the station alongside passengers who had also taken shelter.The actor was also spotted carrying a green backpack and a black bag containing his supplies, as he walked past makeshift tents.Coster-Waldau subsequently shared a snapshot of Kyiv's air raid alerts, which remained at red level for three consecutive days, from October 27 to October 29.Explaining his visit, the actor said he wanted to raise awareness and ensure that the international community continued to pay attention to Ukraine.He said he was there to make sure that “people don’t forget there’s a country in need.”“They’re doing amazing but they need help from the international community, especially now that we’re getting closer to winter,” he added.Despite spending the night in difficult circumstances, Coster-Waldau appeared to remain in good spirits in the photographs, even smiling as he tried to get comfortable on his cot.Coster-Waldau is widely recognised for portraying Jaime Lannister in HBO's fantasy drama Game of Thrones, which ran for eight seasons between 2011 and 2019.His performance earned him two Emmy nominations in the Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series category, in 2018 and 2019.Beyond acting, he has served as a UNDP Goodwill Ambassador since 2016, supporting initiatives related to climate action and gender equality.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Woman Goes Viral After Discovering The Man She's Dating Has Her Saved As 'Cousin Andy,' Speculating She Was 'The Other Woman'
articles.summary: A woman was on a date and sent a text to the man she was seeing. However, when the text popped up on his phone, she saw that he had her saved as the contact...
articles.body:
A woman has sparked viral discourse online after revealing how she discovered that a man she was dating was allegedly hiding their relationship from another woman.

During their date, she sent him a text message and noticed that he had saved her contact information under the name "Cousin Andy," leading her to suspect that he was attempting to conceal their interactions from a girlfriend or wife.

Her account of the suspicious discovery quickly went viral, garnering more than 1.8 million views on TikTok in approximately one month.

The story was shared by Emily, known online as @croupmushroom, a social media content creator who specializes in short, fast-paced storytime videos. Her content primarily consists of personal anecdotes about unusual, humorous or frustrating experiences, which she recounts directly to the camera.

Emily's straightforward delivery and tendency to get to the point quickly have become defining features of her videos, several of which have previously attracted widespread attention online.

One of Emily's latest videos follows her usual storytelling format, focusing on an uncomfortable realization she had while out on a date.

After noticing the unusual name attached to her contact information on the man's phone, she began questioning why he would disguise her identity rather than save her under her actual name.

Emily interpreted the discovery as evidence that he was supposedly already involved with someone else and was attempting to keep their date a secret, turning what might otherwise have been an ordinary romantic outing into another unexpected story for her followers.

The video starts with Emily speaking to the camera while sitting on a couch in a dimly lit room.

"On a date with a man tonight," she says, "And as we were in his car, he asked me to text him something to remind him for later."

"So I did do that," Emily continues, "And then after I did that, I watched my notification pop up on his phone."

"And he had my name saved as Cousin Andy," Emily states, pausing and nodding.

"So," she says, "if your boyfriend or husband has been texting his cousin Andy a whole lot, that would be me."

"And if you go to jail, I will bail you out," Emily adds, "and I'm really sorry," she concludes.

In the comments, people complained about men who cheated on their girlfriends and expressed that they supported Emily for posting the video. Other commenters talked about the times they were in similar situations.

One particular comment brought up how odd it is that infidelity continues to happen in a society where open relationships and polyamorous relationships have become a little more common: "Cheating in 2026 is INSANE. There's poly people literally everywhere. If that's what you want go get it consensually. Break up with the monogamous person if that isn't your vibe. Like why is this hard for people?" they wrote.

In the following days, Emily also did a follow-up video, where she says that she found her date's long-time girlfriend and told her what happened.

articles.title: Angel Studios Banning Sex Scenes, F-Words and Misuse of God’s Name in Movies
articles.summary: Angel Studios is introducing a broad new content policy that bans on-screen sex, nudity, F-words and misusing the name of God. The studio, known for films su...
articles.body:
Angel Studios is introducing a broad new content policy that bans on-screen sex, nudity, F-words and misusing the name of God. The studio, known for films such as the hit "Sound of Freedom," will also give its paying members a chance to vote on movies and TV shows to ensure that a majority of members approve of the content.

Angel's co-founder and chief content officer Jeff Harmon announced "The Angel Promise" in a Fox News interview Thursday, explaining why the studio is taking the strong approach. "I think Hollywood generally kind of lives in a bubble. These are excellent craftsmen. They're the best storytellers in the world. Hollywood has built the best storytelling infrastructure in the world. But at the same time, they've kind of drifted more and more away from the values-based audience that they used to serve."

The new policy introduces three commitments from Angel regarding audience approval of content, strict standards for sex and language and expanded parental controls.

"We promise there's never going to be nudity, and there'll never be sex on screen," Harmon said in the video, explaining that Angel is a "faith-friendly studio."

"No sex acts on screen — ever" reads the pledge on the Angel Studios website , "No F words. And no profanity in titles submitted for young kids (12 and under). Angel will not release original films or series that misuse God's name."

Harmon says the Angel Guild numbers approximately 3 million paying members. The new policy requires that films and television series receive a score of at least 70 out of 100 from members to be included in Angel's programming.

"This is the first time in history that a major Hollywood studio, or top 10 studio in the United States, has come and said, we're going to let the audience have a veto right," Harmon told Fox.

Angel Studios releases include "Runner, "Young Washington" and "David." Upcoming titles include "Drummer Boy," "Angel and the Badman" and "Zero A.D.: The Birth of Christ."

articles.title: Barbara Barrie's daughter Jane Harnick recalls mother's decision to end her life with medical assistance at 95 after terminal cancer diagnosis, reveals her final words to family: 'She was ready to go'
articles.summary: Veteran actress Barbara Barrie, best known for her roles in 'Suddenly Susan' and 'Breaking Away', chose to end her life with medical assistance at her
articles.body: Veteran actress Barbara Barrie, best known for her roles in 'Suddenly Susan' and 'Breaking Away', chose to end her life with medical assistance at her Manhattan home after being diagnosed with terminal cancer. The 95-year-old's decision was supported by her family, with her daughter, actress Jane Harnick, opening up about how her mother approached her final days and why they stood by her choice.Speaking to Page Six, Jane revealed that her mother had believed in the right to medical aid in dying long before her cancer diagnosis. She said Barrie had always been clear about how she wanted to spend her final moments and was grateful that New York's Medical Aid in Dying Act had come into effect just in time for her to exercise that choice.Barbara Barrie's daughter says family supported her decisionRecalling her mother's long-held views, Jane said Barrie had often spoken about wanting to pass away peacefully rather than endure a prolonged illness."For years and years, her whole life before she was ever sick with any illness, she always used to say, 'When my time comes, I just want to take something and go to sleep,'" Jane told Page Six.She added that her mother strongly believed medical aid in dying was a human right. Before the law was introduced in New York, Barrie had even considered travelling to Switzerland or Vermont, where the option was legally available.Jane also spoke about her mother's gratitude towards New York Governor Kathy Hochul, who signed the Medical Aid in Dying Act in January. The legislation officially came into effect in August, allowing eligible terminally ill adults to request life-ending medication through their doctors."She was so grateful that it had been instituted in New York State really in the nick of time," Jane said.'She was ready to go': Daughter recalls mother's final daysBarrie was diagnosed with terminal cancer earlier this month, and her health deteriorated rapidly. According to Jane, the actress was admitted to hospital around three weeks before her death, where she was informed that she could exercise her choice under the new legislation.Despite her diagnosis, Barrie remained involved in decisions surrounding her final days. She continued reading the news, listening to her favourite radio station and even participated in planning her memorial service."We were planning her death and her memorial at the same time and she was fine with it," Jane recalled, adding that her mother had opinions about who should speak and what music should be played."She was ready to go. She knew 95 was old enough," she added.Jane also revealed that her mother began experiencing pain on her final day, and the family and medical team were able to coordinate the process accordingly.Barbara Barrie's final words to her familyThe actress died at her Manhattan home on Wednesday, surrounded by her daughter Jane, son Aaron Harnick and son-in-law Adam Freifeld.Recalling their final moments together, Jane said the family told Barrie they loved her as she was falling asleep. The actress responded, "I love you too." Those were reportedly her last words.Before her death, Barrie had also expressed a wish for her family to continue advocating for medical aid in dying."She was an advocate for a lot of things during her life, and to go out on this one is what she would have wanted," Jane said.Emphasising that the decision was entirely her mother's, Jane added, "She had the most incredible life, she did everything she wanted to do, she had the family she wanted. It was 100 percent her decision, and we all supported it."Barbara Barrie was an accomplished American actress whose career spanned theatre, television and films. She was widely recognised for her performances in 'Breaking Away' and the sitcom 'Suddenly Susan'. Beyond acting, she was also a passionate advocate for medical aid in dying, a cause she remained committed to throughout her life.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.standfirst: La cantante se dio a conocer gracias a 'Operación Triunfo'
articles.summary: La cantante se dio a conocer gracias a 'Operación Triunfo'
articles.body: Hoy visitará 'Pasapalabra' la cantante Lorena Gómez, quien saltó a la fama por quedar primera en la edición de 'Operación Triunfo' del año 2006, programa que, por cierto, hasta hace dos años dirigía el ahora presentador del famoso concurso Antena 3, Roberto Leal. A Lorena le acompañarán otros tres invitados que se sentarán en las sillas de 'Pasapalabra' desde este 3 diciembre y hasta el próximo viernes 5. De esta manera, durante estas tres jornadas pondrán a prueba sus conocimientos y su rapidez en las diferentes pruebas, para ayudar a los concursantes a acumular segundos para el rosco final. Lorena Gómez nace en Lérida en el año 1986, y desde muy pequeña tuvo claro que quería ser una artista. Siendo una niña pudimos verla concursando en programas de Antena 3 como 'Menudas estrellas' y 'Menudo Show', imitando a una de sus referentes, Marifé de Triana. Y es que, a pesar de que formó parte del grupo góspel, la copla es una de sus pasiones. En 2006, su vida cambiaría para siempre. Lorena, que trabajaba como dependiente en una conocida tienda de ropa, labor que compaginaba con el de camarera de una discoteca, decidió lanzarse a la aventura de 'Operación Triunfo'. La joven es admitida como una de las 16 nuevas concursantes de la temporada, y gracias a sus magníficas actuaciones y a su alegre personalidad logra salir como vencedora. Salir como ganadora de 'OT' le permitió arrancar una carrera en solitario, con la que acabaría grabando dos álbumes y varios singles. No obstante, su carrera como cantante la combinará con la televisión y su amor por la interpretación. En el mundo de la pequeña pantalla, destaca su participación en 'Los mejores años de nuestra vida', un divertido programa emitido en La 1. Respecto a la interpretación, participó en el talent show 'Tu cara me suena' en el año 2016, además de protagonizar varias series como actriz en Latinoamérica entre las que sobresalen 'El rostro de la venganza' o 'Marido de alquiler'.

articles.title: Lisa Rinna channels Kylie Jenner, Carson Daly nails Ella Langley's fringe and more: The best celebrity Halloween costumes of 2026 so far
articles.summary: From pop star tributes and family costumes to a wearable seating chart, celebrities are getting into the Halloween spirit.
articles.body:
Is it really Halloween if celebrities don't go all out with their costumes? The spookiest night of the year is just around the corner — which means everyone from actors and artists to athletes and public figures is showcasing their latest looks on social media. Whether it's an obscure, avant-garde take on a larger concept or a faithful — and playful — transformation into a fellow celebrity, the stars have a knack for dressing up.

Below, Yahoo has rounded up the best Halloween costumes of 2026 — so far.

Paris Hilton continued her tradition of dressing up as Britney Spears , this time recreating the pop star's look in the "I'm a Slave 4 U" music video. Hilton also included her family in this year's costumes. The Simple Life star, her husband Carter Reum and their two children brought characters from Beauty and the Beast to life. Reum was the Beast, son Phoenix was Lumiere, daughter London was Chip and Hilton was Belle — a decision that garnered backlash online . Those weren't their only costumes, though: Hilton also dressed up as goth matriarch Morticia Addams, while her hubby and kiddos rounded out the Addams family.

Ticketmaster… but make it wearable? Lily Allen dressed up as the ticketing platform's infamous seating map, wearing a matching white puffer and leotard covered with little blue dots. (We can't get over the "Stage" detail across the collar.) Allen shared her costume on Instagram with the caption, "Never beating the allegations. #bluedotfever." One fan explained the West End Girl singer's costume in the comments.

"For anyone who is missing the joke - Lily canceled her Auckland concert due to being sick," she wrote. "People online said it was because she didn't sell enough tickets. Geddit now? 🫩"

During Friday's broadcast, the Today show hosts debuted their transformations for this year's festivities. Standout costumes included Savannah Guthrie as an old-school news anchor, Al Roker as Gumby and Jenna Bush Hager as Phoebe Buffay from Friends . Our personal favorite? Carson Daly, who dressed up as "Choosin' Texas" hitmaker Ella Langley. Daly hilariously brought the country darling to life — complete with her signature fringe.

Kim Kardashian doesn't play when it comes to Halloween. This year, the Skims founder dressed up as someone near and dear to her heart: her daughter North West! From her long, electric-blue hair and piercings to her signature hand-covering-mouth pose, Kardashian was the spitting image of North.

Keke Palmer and her son, Leodis, channeled 1995-era Janet Jackson and Michael Jackson from their acclaimed "Scream" music video. Palmer transformed into the "All for You" singer, while 3-year-old Leodis made an adorable King of Pop.

"Another memory with mommy and son! I LOVE YOU SO MUCH BUDDY. ITS SO MUCH FUN PLAYING WITH YOU! You will take over the family business, your way, someday," Palmer wrote on Instagram. "My SCREAM come true. 🥹🖤"

They're going stateside! Overcompensating stars Owen Thiele and Benito Skinner dressed up as PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson from their "Stateside" music video. Thiele transformed into the British R&B singer, while Skinner channeled the Swedish pop girlie. The costars pulled out all the stops — from their impeccable glam to their bedazzled "Stateside" crop tops. Their costume even caught Larsson's attention: The "Midnight Sun" singer commented "Ateeeee" on the duo's joint Instagram post.

Kylie Jenner, is that you?! Lisa Rinna transformed into the Khy founder for this year's festivities. Rinna recreated Jenner's look from the Marty Supreme premiere in December 2025: a bright orange Chrome Hearts column gown paired with her signature long black locks.

Calling all Spy Kids fans! This year, model Alex Consani transformed into a Thumb-Thumb, one of the creatures from the 2001 flick starring Daryl Sabara and Alexa PenaVega. In addition to having human-sized thumbs as heads, arms and legs — the memorable henchmen also wore red suits.

Leeloo, is that you? Model Cara Delevingne transformed into Leeloo, the powerful being sent to Earth in the film The Fifth Element . Actress Milla Jovovich famously portrayed the character in the 1997 sci-fi flick.

Count on Liz Gillies to make a stellar pop culture reference. The former Nickelodeon star, who's known for debuting elaborate costumes alongside bestie Ariana Grande , transformed into Luke from Halloweentown .

Love Island USA star Serena Page made the ultimate 2000s Disney Channel reference. Page transformed into Raven-Symoné circa her That's So Raven era — and even recreated one of the show's promotional photoshoots.

Troye Sivan brought a beloved Disney character to life. The "Party" singer stepped out as Woody from the Toy Story franchise.

For their annual Wondaween Festival in Los Angeles, Janelle Monae transformed into "Phish Boy," a fishy sea creature.

"I'm choosing to be courageous and transform," they said during the event. "How do I get to the next version of Janelle?"

McCall DaPron channeled her inner Jackie Kennedy. The star of Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County , which premieres on Nov. 12, her husband, Kirk DaPron and their four children dressed up as the Kennedy family.

articles.summary: Selma Blair on Friday broke her silence weeks after being arrested for alleged assault.
articles.body: Selma Blair on Friday apologized following her arrest after an alleged altercation with flight attendants on a Delta flight earlier this month. The 54-year-old actress said her lawyers had advised her not to say anything because of the ongoing legal matter, but added that she could say: "Not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life. And so to the people I disappointed, that I hurt, I frightened, alarmed I am so sorry." In the emotional Instagram video, taken in what appeared to be her home, she added that she would be taking care of her health and her son "and thinking of you all with gratitude and love." Blair was arrested for assault and arraigned on Monday, Oct. 12, on two counts of second-degree assault stemming from alleged attacks on a Port Authority police officer and a nurse following her arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport from Los Angeles. Police had responded to a call about a "physically abusive passenger" aboard Delta Flight 938. SELMA BLAIR'S REP SPEAKS OUT AFTER STAR'S ARREST: ‘MUCH MORE TO THIS STORY’ Blair pleaded not guilty. The judge set bail at $20,000 cash/$60,000 bond/ $60,000 partially secured bond. She's expected in court in January 2027. "On Sunday October 11 at approximately 11pm at JFK Airport, PAPD responded to a call about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Airlines flight 938 which was parked at the gate after arrival from LAX," New York Port Authority officials confirmed to Fox News Digital. "Suspect was identified as Selma Blair, a 54-year-old woman. She was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation." According to court documents, Blair was restrained on a stretcher at the airport but freed her leg, and allegedly kicked an officer in the face, neck and chest, causing substantial swelling. A nurse at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center, where Blair was taken, alleged that the actress kicked her in the chest while moving her. Delta confirmed that law enforcement officials responded to an incident upon arrival to John F. Kennedy International Airport, a flight which departed out of Los Angeles earlier in the day. "Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first," Delta said in a statement. Sources told TMZ that Blair allegedly punched one flight attendant and bit another in the middle of the flight. Law enforcement officials confirmed Blair was also separately served with a summons by the FBI, and is currently facing one charge of assault. "Since Sunday night, the public account of what happened to Selma aboard a flight to New York has been built almost entirely on a police statement and a decade-old headline," the spokesperson said. "A handful of journalists have taken the time to report on Selma as a human being rather than a headline, and we are grateful to them," the statement continued. "But fair reporting has been the exception, and in the space left by our silence, speculation has hardened into something being treated as fact. articles.title: Karan Johar to attend 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai' 30th anniversary screening at Edinburgh Film Festival
articles.summary: Karan Johar's directorial debut, 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai', starring Shah Rukh Khan, Kajol and RMukerji, will mark its 30th anniversary with a special
articles.body: Karan Johar's directorial debut, 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai', starring Shah Rukh Khan, Kajol and RMukerji, will mark its 30th anniversary with a special screening at the Edinburgh International Film Festival (EIFF) in 2028.Director Karan Johar has accepted the festival's invitation to attend the special screening, which will mark three decades since the film's release.The invitation was extended earlier this week during a meeting at the Mumbai offices of Johar's production banner, Dharma Productions, as per Variety.Scotland's First Minister John Swinney and David Smith, interim executive director of Screen Scotland, met Johar to discuss opportunities for collaboration between Scotland and the Indian film and television industries.The discussions covered Scotland's potential as a filming destination and production partner, including co-productions, talent development and cultural exchange.Confirming Johar's participation, Swinney said, "It was a pleasure to meet Karan Johar in Mumbai, and I am delighted that he has accepted the Edinburgh International Film Festival's invitation to celebrate the 30th anniversary of 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai' which holds a special place in the hearts of communities across Scotland and beyond. I look forward to welcoming him to Edinburgh," as per Variety.He also highlighted the potential for future partnerships between the two film industries, saying, "Scotland's screen industry has tremendous potential as a creative partner for Indian film and television, offering the infrastructure, expertise and world-class filming locations to support a wide range of productions."Released in 1998, 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai' was Johar's first film as a director. The romantic drama featured Shah Rukh Khan as Rahul, a widower whose young daughter helps him reconnect with Anjali, played by Kajol. Anjali had been his college best friend and secretly loved him before he married Tina, portrayed by Rani Mukerji. Salman Khan also appeared in the film as Anjali's fiance.Scotland played a significant role in the film's visual identity. The production filmed at several locations across the country, including Eilean Donan Castle, Glen Coe, Tantallon Castle and Inchmahome Priory.The film's extensive use of Scottish locations helped establish a lasting connection between Scotland's landscapes and mainstream Indian cinema. No major Indian production before 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai' had filmed as widely across Scotland.Other guests are also expected to join the anniversary screening. However, the dates for the 2028 edition of the Edinburgh International Film Festival have not yet been announced.Before the planned celebration, EIFF will mark its 80th anniversary from August 12 to 18, 2027. Submissions for the edition are scheduled to open in January, with further details expected in the coming months.The upcoming milestone celebrations follow the festival's revival in 2024 under Ridd and festival producer Emma Boa. articles.summary: Blair pleaded not guilty and was released on bail after allegedly punching a flight attendant, biting a crew member and assaulting a nurse and a police offic...
articles.body:
Selma Blair is speaking out on camera for the first time after she allegedly assaulted crew members on a Delta flight to New York City's John F. Kennedy Airport on Oct. 11

" I'm sorry that it's taken this long," Blair said in a video posted to Instagram on Friday, Oct. 30

The actress appeared in court on Oct. 12 to plead not guilty to two counts of second-degree assault, and was subsequently released on bail

Selma Blair is apologizing after her Oct. 11 arrest.

The actress, 54, fought back tears as she addressed her followers on Instagram on Friday, Oct. 30, speaking on camera for the first time about the events that led to her arrest on assault charges following a Delta flight to New York City's John F. Kennedy Airport.

The actress appeared in court on Oct. 12 and pleaded not guilty to two counts of second-degree assault; she was released on bail.

"I know I've been quiet for a couple weeks since October 11th," Blair told her followers. "And you deserve to hear from me directly. And I'm sorry that it's taken this long."

Blair said that since there is a "legal matter going on," her lawyers have asked her to keep quiet.

"And I take this very seriously. What I can tell you, though, is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself, in that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life," she said.

"And so, to the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, that I frightened, alarmed. I am so sorry," continued Blair. "And to the people that have written, or called, or sent wishes of love or caring, it has meant everything to me and my son, who is my world, as a scout who is also okay. So right now, I'm going to be taking care of my health and my son, and thinking of you all with gratitude and love."

Blair's comments follow a statement she released to PEOPLE via a representative claiming that "the public account of what happened to Selma aboard a flight to New York has been built almost entirely on a police statement and a decade-old headline."

Blair is accused of punching a flight attendant and biting another crew member during the flight. She is also alleged to have assaulted a nurse and a Port Authority Police officer.

Blair allegedly kicked a registered nurse in the chest at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center at approximately 2 a.m. on Oct. 12, while the nurse was assisting with Blair's transport for further medical treatment, according to according to a criminal court affidavit sworn by Port Authority Police Officer Dynosoph Telisma. The nurse reported substantial pain to her chest, and was granted an order of protection.

Her previous statement alleged that she " experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition."

Her attorney Shawn Barnes told the New York Post and the New York Daily News that it was "not an intentional assault" as she had missed doses of her medication and had maintained a busy work schedule.

A source close to the actress previously told PEOPLE that she is embarrassed and upset following the incident.
