articles.title: Leclerc sets pace in Friday practice at Mexico City Grand Prix
articles.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc goes fastest in Friday practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc headed McLaren's Lando Norris in Friday practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who is poised to clinch his first world title on Sunday, was fourth fastest behind team-mate George Russell.

Only a victory by Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can theoretically stop Antonelli becoming champion on Sunday. Even then, Antonelli only needs ninth place if Russell wins and 10th if Hamilton does.

Leclerc, who topped both sessions on Friday, was 0.103 seconds quicker than Norris, with Russell just 0.003secs further adrift.

Antonelli was 0.217secs off the pace, and ahead of the Red Bulls of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

Leclerc's team-mate Lewis Hamilton was 11th overall after stopping on track with a technical problem before completing his qualifying simulation runs on the soft tyre.

Behind Hadjar, Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson sandwiched Pierre Gasly's Alpine, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri completed the top 10.

Verstappen and Lawson face a trip to the stewards after a collision in the stadium early in the session.

"I don't think it's called unlucky," said Verstappen. "Maybe not very smart behaviour what he was trying to do there.

"At the end of the day it is not going to change my weekend, but if I were him I would act a little smarter and when you're fighting for your seat it's not very smart behaviour."

Lawson is one of three drivers competing for two seats at Racing Bulls, Red Bull's junior team, next year, alongside current team-mate Arvid Lindblad and Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov.

Verstappen added: "When he saw me coming, he suddenly started to accelerate. I don't know what was going through his head, that he wanted to drive me off the track in the hairpin.

"That's not very sensible behavior from someone in his position, to pick a fight with me."

The first session was marked by 10 of the 11 teams running 'rookie' drivers in their cars.

One of them was Cadillac's Colton Herta, who the team are considering promoting to a race seat in place of Valtteri Bottas next season.

Initially, the team felt his running in Mexico had given him enough points under the F1 system to earn a 'superlicence', which is required to race in F1.

But further investigation by governing body the FIA revealed the American nine-time Indycar race winner is still one point short and will have to complete one further practice session this year to secure his licence.

The team plan to do that before the end of the season.

articles.title: Carioca Matsuri: Festival de cultura japonesa chega ao Riocentro | G1
articles.standfirst: Festival será realizado entre sábado (31) e segunda-feira (2), na Zona Sudoeste do Rio. Programação inclui oficinas gratuitas, apresentações musicais, exposição de armaduras, concurso de cosplay e experiências para crianças.
articles.summary: O festival Carioca Matsuri ocupa o Riocentro com oficinas gratuitas, shows de anime, gastronomia de chef Michelin e um grande concurso de cosplay com prêmios em dinheiro.
articles.body:
Carioca Matsuri — Foto: Divulgação/@williansantosfotografo

O Carioca Matsuri será realizado entre sábado (31) e segunda-feira (2), no Riocentro, na Zona Sudoeste do Rio. O festival terá apresentações musicais, oficinas de cultura japonesa, concurso de cosplay, exposição de armaduras e atividades ligadas a animes e games.

O evento ocupará uma área de mais de 11 mil metros quadrados e terá programação diária das 11h às 22h. Segundo a organização, a expectativa é receber cerca de 35 mil pessoas nos três dias .

Entre as atrações estão apresentações de taikô (tambores japoneses), danças tradicionais, shows de músicas de animes, encontros com dubladores e atividades ligadas ao universo dos games.

Veja abaixo o que encontrar no festival.

Um dos espaços gastronômicos será comandado pelo chef André Kawai, que tem uma estrela Michelin e recebeu do governo japonês o título de Embaixador da Boa Vontade para a Difusão da Culinária Japonesa.

O cardápio anunciado inclui pratos como chirashizushi, tendon, combinados de sushi, sashimis e hand rolls. Entre os ingredientes selecionados estão atum bluefin, vieiras de Hokkaido, enguia japonesa, caviar de mujol espanhol e hamachi.

O festival também terá um Auditório Gastronômico, com a participação de chefs e especialistas em culinária japonesa. Estão previstas oficinas gratuitas com demonstrações de técnicas e preparos.

A participação nas atividades será por ordem de chegada, sem necessidade de inscrição antecipada, e estará sujeita à capacidade de cada espaço.

Os fãs de animações japonesas poderão acompanhar apresentações de artistas ligados às trilhas sonoras de animes e participar de encontros com dubladores.

Entre os convidados estão Guilherme Briggs, Wendel Bezerra, Feh Dantas, Tati Keplmair e Vyni Takahashi.

O grupo YuYu20, responsável por versões brasileiras das músicas do anime Yu Yu Hakusho, também está confirmado. Já o cantor Rodrigo Rossi apresentará o espetáculo “Esferas do Zodíaco”, em homenagem aos 40 anos de Os Cavaleiros do Zodíaco e Dragon Ball.

A programação inclui ainda apresentações de grupos dedicados à cultura de Okinawa, com performances de taikô e danças tradicionais.

Concurso de cosplay terá prêmio de R$ 15 mil

O público poderá participar dos desfiles diários de cosplay, com inscrições realizadas no próprio local.

No sábado (31), haverá uma categoria especial de Halloween, para personagens e caracterizações inspirados na data.

O festival também receberá o Mega Cosplay , concurso com premiação total de R$ 15 mil. O vencedor receberá R$ 8 mil. O segundo colocado ganhará R$ 4 mil, o terceiro, R$ 2 mil, e haverá ainda um prêmio de R$ 1 mil para o destaque.

A programação terá também a presença do criador de conteúdo Rodrigo Coelho, conhecido como “ Coelho no Japão ”, que será o embaixador otaku do evento.

Exposição de armaduras, games e atividades para crianças

Dança — Foto: Divulgação Carioca Matsuri

Quem visitar o festival poderá conferir uma exposição de armaduras inspiradas em figurinos de produções como Jaspion e Kamen Rider Black, organizada pela Sato Company. O espaço terá ainda exibição de trailers e conteúdos relacionados a animes, tokusatsu e cinema asiático.

O público também poderá participar de atividades na Arena Dance Party, com jogos de dança, e no Press Start, espaço dedicado a games e consoles japoneses.

Para as crianças, uma das atrações será o parque inflável Hello Kitty and Friends , com personagens como Hello Kitty, My Melody, Kuromi e Cinnamoroll. O espaço terá escorregador, cama elástica, atividades interativas e área para fotos.

A programação inclui ainda oficinas gratuitas de mangá, origami, pixel art, shūji, oshibana, ikebana e bonsai, além de demonstrações de artes marciais, como judô, karatê, sumô, aikido e kendô.

Outra atividade será o Kimono Experience, espaço em que os visitantes poderão vestir quimonos e yukatas originais do Japão.

Festival terá experiência de realidade virtual

O Carioca Matsuri também terá a Sky Bridge Experience , atração apresentada pela Japan Foundation. Desenvolvida originalmente para planetários no Japão, a experiência foi adaptada para a realidade virtual.

A iniciativa integra a programação de intercâmbio cultural entre Brasil e Japão e reúne tecnologia e manifestações artísticas.

Data: 31 de outubro, 1º e 2 de novembro (sábado, domingo e segunda-feira).

Local: Riocentro, na Barra Olímpica, Zona Sudoeste do Rio.

Endereço: Avenida Salvador Allende, 6.555.

Gratuidade: crianças de até 10 anos e 11 meses não pagam, desde que acompanhadas de um adulto pagante.

articles.body:
Alaíde Costa faz feat com Emicida na música 'Só por isso eu vim', parceria dos artistas — Foto: Fábio Audi / Divulgação

♬ Terceiro título da trilogia fonográfica idealizada por Emicida e Marcus Preto para abastecer a discografia de Alaíde Costa com músicas inéditas, o álbum “Meu vício na dor de amar demais” tem lançamento agendado para 26 de novembro.

Vinte dias antes, em 6 de novembro, chega aos aplicativos de áudio o primeiro single do álbum. A música escolhida para abrir os trabalhos promocionais do álbum “Meu vício na dor de amar demais” é uma parceria de Alaíde com o próprio Emicida, “Só por isso eu vim”, gravada pela cantora carioca com o rapper paulistano em feat inédito.

Batizado com o nome de música composta por Guilherme Arantes em parceria com Nando Reis, o álbum “Meu vício na dor de amar demais” inclui no repertório inteiramente inédito um samba-canção de Adriana Calcanhotto, “A falta que não me faz”.

Gravado no estúdio Da Pá Virada, em São Paulo (SP), com músicos como Fábio Sá (baixo) e Pupillo (bateria), o álbum “Meu vício na dor de amar demais” fecha a trilogia composta pelos discos “O que meus calos dizem sobre mim” (2022) e “E o tempo agora quer voar” (2024).

articles.title: Aos 91 anos, Claudette Soares faz feats com Joaquim, Maria Gadú e Thalma de Freitas no álbum 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar' | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista canta músicas inéditas de Leoni e Joyce Moreno no disco programado para 13 de novembro.
articles.summary: Artista canta músicas inéditas de Leoni e Joyce Moreno no disco programado para 13 de novembro.
articles.body:
Claudette Soares na foto da capa 'O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar', previsto para ser lançado em 13 de novembro — Foto: Fábio Audi / Divulgação

♬ Nascida em 31 de outubro de 1935, na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ), a cantora Claudette Soares completa 91 anos hoje, sábado, de olho no futuro. Daqui a duas semanas, precisamente em 13 de novembro, a artista lançará o álbum “O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar”, batizado com bordão a que Claudette sempre recorreu ao longo da carreira.

Além do já conhecido dueto da cantora com Guilherme Arantes na canção “O prazer de viver para mim é você” (2024), Claudette faz feats com Joaquim, Maria Gadú e Thalma de Freitas ao longo das dez faixas do álbum arquitetado por Marcus Preto em 2023 e gravado ao longo dos últimos três anos, na cidade de São Paulo (SP), com produção orquestrada por Preto com Thiago Big Rabello.

Joaquim participa de “Esse escurinho e você”, primeira parceria do artista com Roberto Menescal. Gadú divide com Claudette o canto de “Batuque bom”, parceria de Marcos Valle com Tim Bernardes. Já o feat com Thalma de Freitas acontece em “Viva”, outra música de Marcos Valle, desta vez em parceria com Arnaldo Antunes.

Thalma de Freitas também assina uma das dez músicas do repertório inédito, “O que aconteceu”. Já Leoni contribuiu com a também inédita canção “A vida é bem maior”. Outra novidade é “Esquecível”, parceria póstuma de Joyce Moreno com João Donato (1934 – 2023).

Aliás, “O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar” é o primeiro álbum gravado por Claudette Soares somente com músicas inéditas na discografia iniciada em 1954 com a edição de single de 78 rotações.

“Bem feliz” (Zé Manoel e Ronaldo Bastos) e “Natural” (Zé Renato e Nando Reis) completam o repertório de “O mundo é ruim para quem não sabe esperar”, álbum cuja capa expõe Claudette Soares em foto de Fábio Audi, imagem intencionalmente envelhecida para evocar as capas dos antigos LPs.

A propósito, o álbum foi idealizado por Marcus Preto para ser editado futuramente no formato físico de LP – mais uma homenagem para Claudette Soares, cantora que entrou em cena na adolescência, por volta de 1947, em programas de rádio.

A menina que seria coroada Princesinha do Baião na década de 1950, por ninguém menos do que Luiz Gonzaga (1912 – 1989), transitaria a partir dos anos 1960 por bossa nova, Tropicália, sambalanço, Pilantragem, samba-rock e samba-canção, sempre mostrando bom domínio do ritmo e uma voz afinada em discografia que merece mais reconhecimento.

articles.body: Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' continues its impressive box office journey, with the film approaching the Rs 800 cr worldwide mark. The sequel has also widened its lead over the 2023 release 'Jailer', recording a difference of more than Rs 240 cr at the corresponding stage. However, its latest domestic earnings witnessed a decline compared with the previous day.On Day 16, 'Jailer 2' collected Rs 5.50 cr net across India from 8,079 shows. Its cumulative domestic net collection has reached Rs 435.40 cr, while the India gross stands at Rs 509.45 cr. The overseas market contributed Rs 3 cr on Friday, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 267.50 cr. The film's worldwide earnings have consequently reached Rs 776.95 cr, according to Sacnilk,'Jailer 2' records a 12% drop in Day 16 collectionThe film registered a 12% decline in domestic collections compared with Thursday's earnings of Rs 6.25 cr. Despite the drop, all four language versions continued to contribute to its theatrical performance.The Tamil version remained the biggest contributor, earning Rs 3.75 cr from 3,796 shows. The Hindi version collected Rs 1 cr across 3,310 screenings. Telugu added Rs 55 lakh from 799 shows, while Kannada contributed Rs 20 lakh through 174 screenings. Tamil alone accounted for 68.2% of the day's domestic earnings.Ticket sales also remained substantial during the latest day. Hindi and Kannada added Rs 10 lakh each, from 258 and 122 shows, respectively.Unlike the sequel, the original film recorded an 11.5% increase on its 16th day compared with the previous day's Rs 3.05 cr. Its cumulative India net collection had reached Rs 302.20 cr, while the domestic gross stood at Rs 350.74 cr. Overseas earnings contributed Rs 183 cr, taking its worldwide gross to Rs 533.74 cr. articles.summary: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan's 'Udta Teer' has entered its second week with an improvement in its box office performance.
articles.body: Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan's 'Udta Teer' has entered its second week with an improvement in its box office performance. The spy comedy has generated Rs 50.03 cr in worldwide gross collections after eight days of its theatrical release. The film's latest domestic earnings also registered a 26.7% increase, offering some relief after consecutive daily declines. With its worldwide collection touching the lower end of its reported budget range, the film is gradually approaching its estimated investment.According to Sacnilk, 'Udta Teer' earned Rs 2.85 cr net in India on Day 8, with screenings across 5,013 shows. Its cumulative domestic net collection has reached Rs 33.75 cr, while the India gross stands at Rs 40.28 cr. Overseas markets contributed Rs 75 lakh on Friday, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 9.75 cr. The film was released in theatres on October 23, 2026.'Udta Teer' records a 26.7% rise in Day 8 collectionThe film registered a noticeable improvement on Friday after witnessing a decline in its daily earnings over the preceding three days. Its latest collection increased by 26.7% compared with Thursday's Rs 2.25 cr. The film had earned Rs 2.65 cr on Wednesday before dropping further the following day.'Udta Teer' began its theatrical run with Rs 4.10 cr net in India. Its collections subsequently increased to Rs 7.25 cr on Saturday and Rs 8.20 cr on Sunday. However, the first Monday brought a sharp decline, with earnings falling to Rs 3.20 cr. Tuesday recorded a marginal improvement with Rs 3.25 cr, followed by successive drops on Wednesday and Thursday.The opening week contributed Rs 30.90 cr to the domestic net total. Friday's performance has taken its second-week collection to Rs 2.85 cr so far.Ayushmann Khurrana's 'Udta Teer' approaches its estimated budgetAccording to NDTV, the film's estimated budget is between Rs 50 cr and Rs 65 cr. This reportedly includes production expenses, prints, advertising and cast salaries. With worldwide gross earnings reaching Rs 50.03 cr, the film has touched the lower end of its estimated budget range. However, gross collections do not represent the producers' actual recovery, as theatrical revenue is shared between exhibitors and distributors.The film's opening-day performance was also below Ayushmann Khurrana's biggest theatrical opener. articles.title: 'I do whatever he wants me to do': Akshay Oberoi on working with Siddharth Anand in 'King'; calls Shah Rukh Khan's work ethic exceptional
articles.summary: Akshay Oberoi has shared his experience of working with Siddharth Anand and Shah Rukh Khan in the upcoming film 'King'.
articles.body: Akshay Oberoi has shared his experience of working with Siddharth Anand and Shah Rukh Khan in the upcoming film 'King'. The actor praised the director's visual sensibilities and his ability to create large-scale commercial entertainers. He also spoke about Shah Rukh Khan's professionalism, dedication and efforts to support his co-stars during filming.In a conversation with Variety, Akshay Oberoi discussed what he has observed while working on the project. He said Siddharth Anand's approach to filmmaking offers valuable lessons, particularly in visual storytelling and action choreography. The actor also expressed admiration for the filmmaker's ability to present performers effectively on screen.Akshay Oberoi admires Siddharth Anand's visual craftAkshay Oberoi said watching Siddharth Anand work has been an experience he continues to learn from. As someone who enjoys cinema, he particularly appreciates the director's attention to visuals and technical presentation.“I learn something from him all the time. I love great visuals as a cinema fan. His visual craft and technical aesthetics are great. He has also got such flair for action and for presenting his actors. I just go and submit to him. I do whatever he wants me to do and however he wants me to look. I just stand there and watch him work,” he said.Why Siddharth Anand's commercial filmmaking stands outThe actor also spoke about the creative effort involved in making mainstream commercial films. He disagreed with the idea that artistic value and technical craftsmanship are primarily associated with independent cinema.Akshay Oberoi pointed to Siddharth Anand's previous projects to explain his appreciation for the filmmaker's work. He highlighted how the director has consistently delivered large-scale entertainers while exploring different approaches to commercial storytelling.“There is really serious art and craft to commercial filmmaking. People think art and craft only belong to independent cinema. It is very untrue. I have worked with all types of filmmakers. Siddharth Anand has been able to execute commercial craft at a high level consistently. From “Bang Bang!” to “War” to “Fighter” and “Pathaan,” he has been constantly pushing the commercial barrier. It is a joy to watch him at work.”Akshay Oberoi praises Shah Rukh Khan's commitmentAkshay Oberoi also had considerable praise for his co-star Shah Rukh Khan. He described the superstar as someone who remains involved in the filmmaking process even on days when he does not have scenes to perform.According to the actor, Shah Rukh Khan's presence helps keep the atmosphere on set positive. He also noted that the superstar willingly steps in to help other performers when they need cues or assistance with off-camera scenes.Explaining what makes Shah Rukh Khan's approach to work distinctive, Akshay Oberoi said his commitment extends beyond his own performance.“It is his commitment. He is there on days when it is not even required. He is not working as an actor that day. He is just calm and there. He is keeping everyone motivated. If someone needs a cue or something off camera, he’ll get up and do it. He shows utmost professionalism and commitment. You can’t make it to Shah Rukh Khan’s level without that. He gives everything to their products and to their cinema. He gives everything to entertain the audience,” he said.Shah Rukh Khan and Suhana Khan lead Siddharth Anand's 'King'Directed by Siddharth Anand, 'King' is an upcoming Hindi-language action thriller scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on December 24, 2026. articles.title: Michael Douglas claims he was not taken seriously despite Oscar win; says people saw him as a ‘TV star'
articles.summary: Veteran actor Michael Douglas, who recently published his memoir, ‘One Helluva Ride,' looked back on his years in the entertainment industry.
articles.body: Veteran actor Michael Douglas, who recently published his memoir, ‘One Helluva Ride,' looked back on his years in the entertainment industry. While giving an interview recently, the actor talked about his career and opened up about how it took him a long time to get to his position and how he had to prove himself in the industry, despite the fact that he had already established his footing in the market.Michael Douglas on how he was only seen as a TV actorDouglas’ success had started off with role in successful TV shows. While talking to GQ, Douglas commented that there were a lot of moments when he was venturing into films where directors would not take him seriously and would often limit him to ‘just’ being a TV actor.Despite his shows having high ratings and viewership, and with him being an Oscar-winning producer, many people still refused to see him beyond that image. Recalling one incident, he opened up about how he faced quite some issues before being cast in ‘Romancing the Stone’. He shared, “I had done four seasons on Streets of San Francisco, which was a big television hit.” He added that screenwriter Diane Thomas, who had been working as a waitress at the time, had brought him the script for ‘Romancing the Stone,' and he recalled that while reading it he believed that the movie was "just magical.” Douglas continued, "It was a romantic adventure comedy with action, almost a mix that was very hard to come by.”Douglas revealed that he never had himself set for the main role of Jack, commenting, “I tried to get a couple of the big actors to do it.” However, almost everyone turned the project down. “The big issue, I guess, of making it was so funny that I’m an Academy Award-winning producer, but as an actor, I was a television actor trying to make the move into feature films. So there were a lot of studios that did not approve me as an actor," he stated.Even after he suggested that he could play the lead, the casting team went with Jeff Bridges, who is best known for his work in ‘True Grit’ and ‘Tron’. However, due to some circumstances, they ended up casting Douglas, and upon its release, the film was a massive hit amongst the masses. According to Box Office Mojo, the film made USD 115 million at the box office.Douglas left the hit TV show ‘Streets of San Francisco’ in its fifth season to produce ‘One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest,' which scored him an Oscar for Best Picture. Before scoring ‘Romancing the Stone,' he also produced ‘The China Syndrome’ in 1979. articles.title: Serie A Preview: Milan vs Inter – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
articles.summary: One of the most interesting fixtures in the Serie A calendar takes place at San Siro this weekend as Milan take on their fiercest rivals, Inter. The latest e...
articles.body:
One of the most interesting fixtures in the Serie A calendar takes place at San Siro this weekend as Milan take on their fiercest rivals, Inter. The latest edition of the famous Derby della Madonnina could already determine the fate of Milan's faint title hopes.

Despite going unbeaten in his first eight league games in charge of Milan (W5, D3), Ruben Amorim is responsible for the club's second-weakest start to the season since 2019/20. Only 18 points from the opening nine rounds left the Rossoneri seven points adrift of joint leaders Inter and Lazio ahead of the weekend.

With that in mind, anything other than a win in this mouth-watering showdown would likely spell the end of Milan's pursuit of their landmark 20th Scudetto. However, it's easier said than done, especially given Inter's form heading into this meeting. Cristian Chivu's men have enjoyed a near-flawless start to their title defense.

Inter left it late to beat out-of-sorts Venezia in midweek Serie A action, as two own goals from the Winged Lions beyond the 75th minute propelled them to a 2-0 victory. The Nerazzurri have dropped points once so far this season (W8, D1) and are currently level on points with Lazio and four clear of third-placed Roma.

Amorim's unbeaten Serie A record ended abruptly on Wednesday as Bologna thrashed Milan 4-2 at San Siro despite trailing by a goal at halftime. Raffaele Palladino's side brutally exposed Milan's defensive frailties, which have seen the Rossoneri concede at least two goals in three of their last four games across all competitions.

San Siro has been anything but a fortress this term, with two of Amorim's three defeats at the helm coming at this stadium (W3). If it's any consolation, Milan have scored two or more goals in four of their five competitive home outings in 2026/27, except for a dismal 2-0 loss to Benfica in the Europa League.

Further confidence could come from the fact that Milan have only lost one of their last 13 home league matches in this kick-off slot (W7, D5). Upholding that promising trend is not beyond the realm of possibility despite their recent struggles, given that the Rossoneri are enjoying their longest unbeaten run in this fixture in more than 20 years.

Though it sounds somewhat paradoxical, Inter have failed to beat Milan in their last seven meetings in all competitions (D2, L5), losing both Serie A encounters last season by a goal to nil. Keen to buck that frustrating trend, the reigning Scudetto holders head into proceedings on the back of their best league start since 1988/89.

Chivu's charges have developed a 'never give up' mentality that puts them in the driver's seat here. For context, they've won a league-high 13 points from losing positions this season (W4, D1), suggesting that no one should dare to write them off even if they concede first in this derby.

Inter have also been too hot to handle in the final third, netting 25 Serie A goals in nine matches, more than any other team. Furthermore, they've been ruthless at San Siro this season, winning all five competitive home matches, which also bodes well, even though they're the designated away side.

Samuel Chukwueze, Mattia Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers, and Ruben Loftus-Cheek will not be at Amorim's disposal on Saturday. However, Diego Moreira, Adrien Rabiot, and Mario Gila could return to the squad after missing the match against Bologna, with the former likely to take Davide Bartesaghi's place on the left wing.

As for Inter, long-term absentees John Stones, Curtis Jones, Luis Henrique, and Benjamin Pavard remain on the sidelines. Yet, the absence of captain Lautaro Martinez is the heaviest blow, with Ange-Yoan Bonny expected to replace him in attack at the expense of Francesco Pio Esposito.

Milan vs Inter Potential Starting Lineups

Milan (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Tomori, De Winter, Pavlovic, Estupinan; Musah, Jashari; Hutchinson, Cisse, Moreira; Ramos.

Inter (3-5-2): Provedel, Augusto, Bisseck, Bastoni; Diouf, Zielenski, Stankovic, Sucic, Dimarco; Bonny, Thuram.

Despite Inter's superior form and attacking firepower, Milan's impressive record in this fixture makes the Derby della Madonnina difficult to call. Amorim's side have struggled defensively in recent weeks, but the potential returns of Rabiot, Moreira, and Gila could provide a timely boost.

A share of the spoils could be on the cards.

articles.title: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta passes away at 57; Kamaal R Khan mourns the 'Kaante' director's demise, says, 'You were so knowledgeable about everything'

articles.body: Sanjay Gupta, the filmmaker known for his crime dramas, urban thrillers and stylised action films, has reportedly passed away. Working as a director, screenwriter and producer, he left a lasting imprint on mainstream Hindi cinema. No cause of death has been shared yet, and the industry is waiting for further word from his family and close associates.How Sanjay Gupta began his directorial career with ‘Aatish’Gupta’s journey as a director began with 'Aatish: Feel the Fire' in 1994, an action drama headlined by Sanjay Dutt and Aditya Pancholi. The film gave audiences their first look at his taste for hard-hitting action, punchy dialogues and stylised storytelling. In the years that followed, he developed a visual style all his own, especially in films set in the world of crime and the Mumbai underworld.Kamaal Khan pays tribute to Sanjay GuptaTaking to X handle, Kamaal Khan confirm the sad news and wrote, "RIP Sanjay Bhai. I love you Sanjay and I will miss you everyday bro."‘Kaante’ remains Sanjay Gupta’s cult heist thriller'Kaante' (2002), which Gupta both directed and produced, is still among his best-known works. This heist thriller brought together Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt, Suniel Shetty, Mahesh Manjrekar, Lucky Ali and Kumar Gaurav. Filmed largely in the United States, it won a cult following over the years for its gritty tone and ensemble storytelling.Sanjay Gupta’s films on the Mumbai underworld and beyondGupta’s career kept circling back to the underworld. articles.body: Former India cricketer Yuvraj Singh has shared an update on his much-anticipated biopic, revealing that filming could begin next year. The former all-rounder discussed the project during an interaction with the media. He also spoke about his experiences with fatherhood, his approach to health and life after retiring from professional cricket.Yuvraj Singh hopes to begin biopic shoot in 2027Yuvraj Singh announced his biopic in 2024, raising expectations among cricket fans and audiences. During the recent conversation, he indicated that the team was hoping to take the project into production next year.“Hopefully we start shooting next year,” he said, offering a brief update on the film's progress in a chat with Mid Day. Although he did not share further details about the production, his remark provides a possible timeline for the project. The biopic is expected to bring important chapters of his life and cricketing career to the screen.Cricketer opens up on his cancer diagnosisYuvraj Singh's career included several memorable achievements, including his remarkable feat of hitting six sixes in an over. However, his journey also involved a difficult personal battle when he was diagnosed with cancer at the height of his cricketing career.The cricketer eventually returned to the field and continued representing India after his treatment. His comeback became one of the defining chapters of his sporting journey. It also inspired people dealing with serious health challenges.Yuvraj Singh stresses the importance of discussing health strugglesDuring the interaction, Yuvraj Singh spoke about why people often hesitate to discuss cancer and other serious illnesses. He recalled being concerned that revealing his diagnosis could affect his cricketing career. He also emphasized the importance of sharing personal experiences and seeking support.“I've been someone whose health fluctuated in the early days of my career. For me, health is wealth. A lot of people are scared of the disease, and even more so of talking about it. There was a time when I didn't want to either, because I knew if I did, maybe my cricket would end. People would think, 'This guy has cancer; he can't play cricket.' I believe my journey has inspired many people to overcome adversity. It's important to share your experiences with others, and you need friends and family to talk about what you're going through, because mental health is a very important aspect of our lives,”Yuvraj Singh made these remarks while attending the launch of Protocol32, a daily health drink.Former India all-rounder opens up about fatherhoodBeyond cricket and his upcoming biopic, Yuvraj Singh also spoke about his personal life. The former India all-rounder is a father of two and described how his children influence his everyday routine.He explained that hearing them in the morning immediately changes his mood and gives him the energy to get out of bed. For him, spending time with his children remains one of the most rewarding experiences.“You see your kids, and the energy just comes out of your body! But the moment I hear my kids talking outside my door in the living room, it’s just pure instinct to jump up and hug them. They come bouncing at you, and it’s probably the best feeling in the world. articles.title: INSIDE Babil Khan’s Lokhandwala home: Indoor swing, ping-pong table, guitar-filled studio bedroom and corner honouring late father Irrfan Khan
articles.summary: Babil Khan’s Mumbai home is warm, artistic and truly lived in.
articles.body: Babil Khan’s Mumbai home is warm, artistic and truly lived in. Filmmaker-choreographer Farah Khan recently visited the house in Lokhandwala with her cook, Dilip, for her vlog. She called it “one of the most beautiful residences” they have seen so far. Babil lives here with his mother, Sutapa, and younger brother, Ayan.A corner for Irrfan KhanThe first thing visitors notice is a special corner for the late actor Irrfan Khan. It has his black-and-white photograph, fresh tuberoses and a framed poster of ‘Qissa’, one of the finest films of his career. A side table in the living room also holds his portrait and a ‘Qissa’ poster, decorated with candles and white flowers.Living room with a wooden swingBefore reaching the door, Farah Khan and Dilip walked through a porch done in red and golden tones, with indoor plants and antique decor. Inside, a large wooden indoor swing with thick ropes sits between the dining and sitting areas. The room has big grey sofas with silver patterned cushions, stylish coffee tables, books, a small stone pond and minimal showpieces. An antique carved wooden panel shaped like a jharokha adds a traditional touch to the main wall.Dining area and ping-pong tableThe dining area has a long wooden table with high-back chairs in floral prints. The walls carry white Bohemian textures and rustic wooden mirrors, the ceiling has a raw concrete finish, and tall windows let in plenty of sunlight. A ping-pong table stands in the middle of the space. When Farah asked whether it was really used, Babil said, “Yes, I play with everyone. We can also play right now.” The area opens to a wide balcony full of green potted plants.Bedroom that doubles as a music studioBabil’s room is part bedroom and part studio, with separate zones for work, sleep and music. His workstation has eight guitars on the wall, along with computers, speakers, a gaming console, a digital piano and other audio gear. He also owns a wooden cajón. The sleeping side has a tall bed with a mural behind it, a utility cart with books and a treadmill. A brown leather massage chair sits in the centre, and a projector hangs from the ceiling. Babil also showed his brother’s music studio.Cooking dahi chickenBabil Khan does not know how to cook, and his mother had just recovered from dengue. So Farah and Dilip taught him their special dahi chicken recipe in the kitchen.Farah Khan and Sutapa Sikdar’s friendshipDuring the vlog, Farah recalled how she met Sutapa on the sets of the Shah Rukh Khan starrer ‘Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa’. She said, “She was a writer but was doing the costume designing of the film to earn money, and I was the choreographer. The production gave a government hostel accommodation to us, where we were sharing a room. We became best friends during that time.”Irrfan Khan’s early days in BollywoodFarah also spoke about Irrfan’s early struggles. “When I was with Sutapa, he was a struggling actor. Sutapa used to give him pocket money. She was investing in his dreams,” she said. Babil agreed and added, “Haan, Dad used to take money from Mom during his NSD days.”Old memories and a playful momentWhile the chicken cooked, Farah and Babil played ping-pong, and then they met Sutapa. The friends sat down to chat and went back to their ‘Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa’ days. Farah said, “I remember you used to give Irrfan pocket money and tell me that your boyfriend was coming to meet you. And a very odd-looking guy would come, sweet only he was.”Sutapa then teased her, saying, “You are still in touch with Sanjay Leela Bhansali. When I met him, he told me that you had a crush on Irrfan.” Farah laughed and denied it. “It’s not true; I was just in love with his work. articles.summary: Discover how Demi Lovato transformed her $7 million LA farmhouse into a colorful, maximalist dream home, complete with unique art, a home studio, and luxury amenities.
articles.body: Demi Lovato quite literally started with a blank slate when she purchased her first real estate property in 2020. The stunning farmhouse estate, located in Studio City, Los Angeles, is one of the most lavish properties in the area and had only recently been built when the homes in the area went up for sale. The singer jumped at the chance, and while at the time things may have been harder than others, she ended up managing to create a stunning place to fit to her liking.Demi Lovato’s LA farmhouse that she bought in 2020The 8,500-square-foot farmhouse estate had been freshly built in the quiet neighborhood of San Fernando Valley and was a brand new start for the singer. Since it was a newly built space at the time, not much personalized work was done on the residence, which ended up working out perfectly for Lovato. She worked with Kat Bell and James Drew of Argyle Design to transform the space into a maximalist and colorful residence that matched her energy and liking. She also did an ‘Open Door’ tour with Architectural Digest to show off her home and how she has been making the building her own.Featuring 6 bedrooms and 9 bathrooms, some of the key exterior features of the property included a saltwater pool, a private spa, a fire pit, an outdoor kitchen, a built-in dog area (for pets Batman and Cinderella), and a pull-down outdoor projector screen visible from the pool or hot tub.The property also has ample space for parking vehicles since the space also features a short gated driveway that is situated right before the two-car garage, along with a longer gated driveway that directly leads to a second garage, which is subterranean with room for up to four luxury vehicles.More about the interiors of Demi Lovato’s USD 7 million LA homeAs for the interiors, the entryway is more minimalist and calm in order to balance the rest of the house's maximalist concept and does not have much decor or color. However, the remainder of the house is a perfect embodiment of Lovato. The singer has an artwork, Untitled RL032, in her home by artist Ko Kirk Yamahira, along with an Ekstrem chair, an Italia travertine table, a black Alvar Aalto stool, and an Ettore doorstop by Magis.There are also mirrored elevator cabs designed to resemble a futuristic spaceship. While the living room features a branded and eccentric sofa and lounge chairs, one of the most eye-catching features of the room is the Zebra onyx crystal lamps, along with the Scraplights by Graypants, a leather pig sculpture, and a fireplace, all of which add some personality to the living space.Lovato has her own ‘shroom room’ as well, which is essentially a space where she rests and relaxes and works on her projects. Featuring artworks and lighting from multiple artists, the room also has a custom modular sofa inspired by Hans Hopfer’s Mahjong sofa for Roche Bobois, alongside tongue-shaped chairs and mushroom-shaped stools. It also has silver walls, glimmering curtains, butt-shaped vases, and anatomical salt/pepper shakers.Lastly, she also had a pool house with the main residence when she bought the property. However, instead of using it as is, Lovato completely converted it into her own home studio. This is where the singer recorded the entirety of her album, ‘Holy Fvck.’ The room is inspired by the 1960s vintage theme and has an old and classic Italian chandelier, iridescent Murano glass discs, an upholstered stool, and a quirky rug.Lovato and Canadian musician and songwriter Jordan "Jutes" Lutes spend their time here. The two tied the knot on May 25, 2025, at the Bellosguardo Estate in Santa Barbara, California. articles.title: Questions still haunt Houdini’s Halloween death 100 years later
articles.summary: Harry Houdini's death 100 years ago was officially blamed on peritonitis, but theories about punches, mediums and murder still fuel debate today.
articles.body: Mystery cloaked the life and performances of escape artist Harry Houdini—and it followed him into his death, perplexing experts for the past century. Houdini, a Hungarian born Erik Weisz, became one of the most famous magicians and vaudeville performers in history after immigrating with his family to the United States at 4. He died 100 years ago on Oct. 31, 1926, at 52. His official cause of death was listed as peritonitis, an infection caused by a ruptured appendix. But since the day he died, theories about alternative causes have lived on. WATCH: HARRY HOUDINI RETURNS FROM THE GRAVE IN AI-GENERATED FOX NATION SERIES 100 YEARS AFTER HIS DEATH Some say a surprise punch to his stomach caused deadly appendicitis to the man who kept himself in peak physical condition. Others insist he suffered from an intestinal blockage. Some theorize that he was killed by people working as spirit mediums. He had been exposing them as frauds just before his death. One of the most widespread myths was caused by a 1953 film in which Houdini was portrayed as unable to escape Water Torture Cell in time to save his own life. "There’s plenty of room for speculation, for conspiracy theories, and so it continues," Houdini historian and biographer John Cox told Fox News Digital. "It continues to this day." Houdini's story returns in the new three-part Fox Nation series "Houdini: Back from the Dead," where artificial intelligence helps him appear to sit down for a modern-day interview to recount his struggles, relationships and legendary feats. ‘Poorly timed’ punch A key event in the timeline of Houdini’s death is the now-famous series of punches to his stomach on Oct. 22, 1926. Nine days before Houdini died, a university student named J. Gordon Whitehead visited the performer in his dressing room at a Montreal theater. Historians report that Houdini was reclining on a couch when Whitehead asked if he could test his ability to withstand a blow to the stomach. Houdini obliged. But before he could brace himself, Whitehead began punching. It continued until another person in the room begged Whitehead to stop, said Roger Dreyer, President of Houdini Revealed, a museum in New York. Many historians agree that because of the punches, Houdini ignored what actually were symptoms of appendicitis, Cox said. Though some believed the blows caused the deadly inflammation, that was never proven. WATCH: Harry Houdini returns in new AI-powered Fox Nation series "He didn't get it treated in time," Cox said. "His appendix ruptured. This caused peritonitis, which was a massive infection. And back then, you died from that. "Had he not been punched, this pain would have come out of nowhere, and he might have gone and sought medical attention sooner. So the punch was very likely just a very poorly timed accident that caused him to not pay attention to what was really happening to him medically." Regardless, the punches brought a financial windfall to his family. Houdini was thousands of dollars in debt at the time of his death. Because the punches were blamed for killing him, his life insurance policy paid out double. "He had a life insurance [policy] of $25,000," Dreyer said. The agreement was that "if he died from an accident, he received another $25,000. Twenty-five-thousand dollars back then was almost $500,000" in today’s value. Spooky Halloween seances Houdini had been fixated on the idea of death, because his daredevil behavior often brought him to the brink of it, Dreyer said. But Houdini also worked to expose as frauds people who claimed to communicate with the dead. He believed their tactics were scams that targeted grieving people. He faced defamation lawsuits for that, Dreyer said. He and his wife, Bess Houdini, made an agreement that if one of them died, they would try to contact the other. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X After his death, Bess Houdini held seances every Halloween for 10 years, attempting to make contact. When none of her attempts were successful, she gave up, concluding contact with the dead wasn’t possible. One hundred years later, interest in Houdini lives on. That’s because he was more than just a performer, Dreyer said. "It's not because of his death we're talking about him. It's because of the way Houdini lived and what he represented. That's why we're talking about Houdini." SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS He was the top "social influencer" of his time––a "pop icon," Dreyer said. Houdini still is a household name and is synonymous with escaping tricky situations, he noted. articles.title: Cornish filmmaker performs live soundtrack to new movie
articles.summary: Mark Jenkin says playing the score live "heightens the emotion" felt by the audience.
articles.body:
Film director Mark Jenkin has been performing a live soundtrack to his new film to "heighten the emotion" felt by the audience as the drama unfolds.

Jenkin's third film is the story of missing fishing trawler Rose of Nevada, which mysteriously returns to a Cornish harbour. Two young men, played by Callum Turner and George MacKay, join its crew unaware how their fates will change.

Jenkin has been performing the score live at theatre screenings with his musical partner Dion Star. They use improvised and composed pieces including tape machines, synths, guitars and field recordings.

He said the soundtrack could change at each showing. "We react to the film live with the audience," Jenkin said.

Jenkin's "creativity" has been praised by music critic Mark Kermode who saw one of the performances.

"Seeing the film with a live music performance is fantastic because they are creating the music right there in front of you.

"It's brilliant, it really adds another dimension to the movie," he said.

Jenkin, who performs with Star under the banner The Cornish Sound Unit, said they "reimagined" the soundtrack each time it was played so it was never exactly the same as it is the film.

"The music in the film is made by me in an idiosyncratic kind of way with lots of tape machines and stuff.

"We reimagine the score live, so it is bigger, because when you are on stage in front of a screen you don't want to not be doing things for large proportions of time," said Jenkin.

He said the music "played along with the audience's reactions".

"We are reacting to the audience - you can feel what direction they are going in, which bits they are finding funny and which bits are feeling emotional - we can heighten that and play with it.

"Sometimes I look to Dion and say we have done something special there. It's transcended what was there before.

"We are very much in the moment when we're doing it."

He said the instruments and techniques used to create the soundtrack had a direction of their own.

"Some is made using tape-to-tape machines. It's like a wild animal, you have no control over it, the only thing you can do is turn it off and we don't do that. It never sounds the same twice."

Jenkin said he liked adding a live element to the film-watching experience.

"The rooms we watch films in we call a cinema. Americans call them movie theatres. I prefer that, I like the idea of it being theatre, with a live element."

But Jenkin said what they were doing was "nothing new" and harped back to the days when a live pianist would play during silent movies.

"From the beginning of cinema to when talkies came in, every film had a live score.

"We are going back to the roots of what the cinematic experience was."

Kermode said he was not the only person who had been absorbed when watching the film with the live soundtrack as musician and radio presenter Jarvis Cocker shared his enthusiasm.

"I was at a showing when Mark was doing a live soundtrack and the really lovely thing was it was packed and at some point Jarvis Cocker came in and was overwhelmed by it. So next time he was on 6 music he played one of the tracks ."

Rose of Nevada, released in 2025, was filmed in Hayle and Mullion in Cornwall and Jenkin has spoken about the challenges that tide and time presented him with.

Newlyn-born Jenkin won a Bafta for his debut Bait in 2020, a film documenting tensions between longstanding and new residents of a Cornish fishing village.

Jenkin said after filming Bait and the 2023 folk horror film Enys Men, which centred on a woman living on a Cornish island, he had said he "didn't want to do anything with boats again".

He had a change of heart however and decided to go ahead with Rose of Nevada, which was all filmed in west Cornwall and premiered at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival.

Since appearing in the film, Turner has been named as one of the favourites to be cast as the next James Bond .

articles.title: Miranda Lambert's friend kidnapped by her own father at age 7 recalls daring rescue that brought her home
articles.summary: Lauren Burns was 7 when her father abducted her from Dallas to Jordan. Miranda Lambert's family helped spark the daring rescue mission home.
articles.body: Lauren Burns was dressed in a cheerleader costume for Halloween weekend in 1987 when she climbed into her father's car. But instead of taking her trick-or-treating, he drove the 7-year-old to the airport and flew her thousands of miles from her Dallas home. Ali Bayan assured the little girl that the trip to his home country of Jordan was a "surprise" — and that her mother, Cathy Mahone, knew all about it. But as days turned into weeks and her father refused to let her speak to her mother, Burns began to realize she might never return home. "I didn't think I would ever see my mother again," Burns recalled to Fox News Digital. MIRANDA LAMBERT, CARRIE UNDERWOOD 'SHOULD GET A RIBBON' FOR SURVIVING COUNTRY MUSIC IN MALE-DOMINATED ERA Burns recounts the abduction and the international rescue mission it sparked in her memoir, "Stolen." Her childhood friend, country music superstar Miranda Lambert — whose family played a crucial role in bringing Burns home — wrote the foreword. Fox News Digital reached out to Lambert for comment. "By the time I was six weeks old, my parents got divorced," Burns said. WATCH: MIRANDA LAMBERT'S FRIEND RECALLS BEING KIDNAPPED BY FATHER AT AGE 7 "All I ever knew was that kind of upbringing. I went between two homes. My mother had full custody of me when I was six weeks old, but she did not want to keep me from my father. He was a good dad. He was loving and kind. I saw him almost every other weekend or maybe extra if she needed help. They had a good relationship despite the reasons that they had gotten divorced." During the drive to the airport, Burns wondered why her stepmother and siblings weren't coming along. "He'd never done anything to make me feel like I couldn't trust him," Burns said. "He was my dad, my provider. He was the one that loved me dearly. So, if he tells me something, I'm going to trust him. But it didn't quite add up." Burns' parents met while Mahone, a Christian, was working as a waitress and Bayan, a Muslim, was studying engineering in Texas. Mahone had full custody, but Bayan, who owned a restaurant in Dallas, saw his daughter regularly. There were "no red flags," Burns said, until that Halloween weekend. The Monday after Halloween weekend, Mahone went to Burns' elementary school to have lunch with her, as she typically did. She expected to hear about her daughter's weekend of trick-or-treating with her father. Instead, she discovered that Burns had never arrived at school. She soon learned that her ex-husband had abducted their daughter and taken her to Jordan. A desperate Mahone rushed to a pay phone. She called the one man she believed could help her: Miranda Lambert's father, Rick Lambert. The former Dallas police officer ran a private detective agency with his wife, Beverly. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "Rick and Beverly were home," Burns said. "They got Miranda, they moved out of their house, and they were with my mom day and night trying to figure out a way to help my mom get me back. They were calling everyone they knew. Rick pulled some strings and got an appointment at the Dallas County Courthouse, so my mom could try to get a warrant out for my father's arrest." The Lamberts had known Mahone for years, long before Burns and Miranda were born. Their friendship began when Mahone worked for Miranda's grandmother, Wanda, at an apartment complex. Until then, Burns had traveled only to Florida to visit her grandmother. Now, the 7-year-old was in the Middle East, unable to speak Arabic and struggling to adjust to unfamiliar customs and a different way of life. "I had to cover my hair," Burns said. "I could not wear shorts. We had to take our shoes off and wash our feet. There were no toilets. It was a hole in the ground with a chain above. I had never seen anything like that. Even the way we ate, it was a communal type of eating. You would sit on the floor with a big rug that was underneath and big plates of food, fresh food. You could smell all the different spices and the fresh hummus. We would all sit together, and you would eat with your hands." But for Burns, the most painful change was in the father she had always trusted. Once in Jordan, the man she viewed as her protector became "distant." articles.summary: Hair and makeup: Makeup by Hillery Written by: Ancela Jamindar From creepy clowns and haunted dolls to iconic Indian horror characters, Halloween always
articles.body: Hair and makeup: Makeup by HilleryWritten by: Ancela JamindarFrom creepy clowns and haunted dolls to iconic Indian horror characters, Halloween always brings out the city's spooky side. While some love recreating their favourite horror characters through elaborate makeovers, others embrace the occasion with themed dinners, gothic aesthetics and nostalgic memories of horror shows that once kept them awake at night. For some, the celebration is also a way to remember loved ones, making Halloween a mix of fright, fun, and personal expression.I am inspired by Pennywise: Shivani JoshiShivani Joshi, inspired by Pennywise from the film It, posed with the iconic red balloon as she recreated a spooky look. She says, “I am dressed as a haunted doll, inspired by Pennywise from the 2017 Hollywood horror film It. This Halloween, I plan to keep things low-key, cosy and chic. I want to create a warm atmosphere with pumpkin lanterns and fairy lights, followed by a Halloween-inspired family dinner featuring red sauce spaghetti, roasted vegetables, and chocolate mousse."She adds, "Annabelle from The Conjuring is the scariest horror character for me. I also enjoy Wednesday for her witty, spooky humour, while I find Munjya mischievous and fun to watch. As a child, I loved watching horror shows, although I was equally scared. I would watch shows like The Zee Horror Show, Mano Ya Na Mano, Woh and Ssshhhh... Koi Hai. After watching Woh, I stopped going anywhere near clowns!"The Stree 2 look will always remain special: Bhumi RajgorStree 2 actress Bhumi Rajgor created the character's signature scary look in a shoot with us. She says, “I’m dressed as Stree, my character in Stree 2, which makes this look particularly special. Stree is the most beautiful woman in the village, but there is much more to her than meets the eye. She is mysterious and powerful, and in her own way, a protector who destroys evil and safeguards the innocent. I think she has become one of the most iconic and beloved Indian horror characters in recent times. So, I’m embracing my inner Stree this year! Halloween is the perfect excuse to dress up, have fun and let your spooky side take over."She adds, "The horror character that scares me the most is Samara from The Ring. There is something deeply unsettling about the way she appears, and her eerie, unpredictable presence stays with you long after the film ends. I think the best horror characters are those that get under your skin without even having to do very much. I have nostalgic memories of watching horror shows as a child. My siblings, cousins, and I would switch off the lights, hide behind pillows, and watch Aahat, The Zee Horror Show and horror films by the Ramsay Brothers. We would be terrified, but we simply couldn’t stop watching! Another funny memory is how we would dress up in scary masks and long, white, flowing clothes, sneak out late at night and stand silently in the middle of the road to scare unsuspecting passersby."Billy the Puppet is one of my favourites: Maulika PatelMaulika Patel, who dressed up as Billy the Puppet from Saw, says, “I love his iconic creepy smile, red bow tie, and mysterious vibe. He looks innocent at first, but there is something terrifying about him. After all, who says a smile can’t be scary?"She adds, "For me, Halloween is more than just a spooky evening. It is also a tribute to the people who are no longer with us. There is something comforting about the belief that, on this evening, the line between the living and the dead becomes thinner. It makes me feel that the people I miss are a little closer to me. At the same time, Halloween is about celebrating life with your people, enjoying music, dressing up as your favourite characters and embracing the gothic aesthetic. Last year, I dressed up as Bellatrix and Morticia Addams. Billy the Puppet is one of my favourites because of his iconic look and the psychological horror associated with him. But if we’re talking about a character who genuinely gives me chills, it has to be Valak from The Conjuring universe. That creepy presence is something else! Also, Aahat and The Zee Horror Show were iconic. They had a different kind of horror, with suspense, haunting background music, and stories that stayed with you long after an episode ended. Indian horror from that era had its own charm. Sometimes, the fear was all about the atmosphere, and that made it even scarier.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Artist explores the many moods of Bombay through seventh solo exhibition
articles.summary: From the rush of local trains and rain-soaked streets to the quiet stretch of the sea, artist Swati Goel turns her attention to the emotional landscape of
articles.body: From the rush of local trains and rain-soaked streets to the quiet stretch of the sea, artist Swati Goel turns her attention to the emotional landscape of Bombay in her seventh solo exhibition, emotions of (BOM)bay. On display at the Nehru Centre’s AC Gallery in Worli, Mumbai, from October 13 to 19, the exhibition explores the city through its contradictions, relationships and everyday experiences.For Goel, Bombay is more than its familiar landmarks or physical geography. It is a city shaped by the people who inhabit it and the emotions they carry through its restless routines. The local trains, for instance, become spaces where ambition, fatigue, hope and resilience intersect, while brief encounters between strangers point to a shared experience of navigating the city.The exhibition also looks at the contrast between the city's constant movement and its quieter moments. Along the coastline, the sea offers a space for reflection and release, providing a counterpoint to the crowded streets and the urgency of urban life.Bombay's contrasts form another thread through the works. Skyscrapers rise alongside densely populated neighbourhoods, prosperity exists alongside hardship, and everyday struggles are often accompanied by unexpected acts of generosity. Rather than reducing the city to a single mood, Goel explores these opposing realities as part of its character.The monsoon, too, features in the artist's interpretation of Bombay. Rain alters the city's colours and rhythms, bringing both disruption and beauty. Romance finds expression in smaller, familiar details: late-night conversations, cutting chai, rain-soaked streets and streetlights. Together, these moments reflect how personal memories and emotions become intertwined with a city's identity.At its heart, emotions of (BOM)bay considers Bombay a city of dreams, shaped by persistence and sacrifice. Through the exhibition, Goel invites viewers to look beyond the idea of the city as a destination and consider it as an emotional experience, where exhaustion and excitement, loneliness and belonging, and despair and hope coexist.The exhibition is open to visitors from 11 am to 7 pm at the Nehru Centre's AC Gallery, Worli, from October 13 to 19.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: London to host nine-day multidisciplinary arts showcase in June 2027
articles.summary: The Serendipity Arts Festival will make its international debut in London from June 19 to 27, 2027, bringing together artists and cultural institutions
articles.body: The Serendipity Arts Festival will make its international debut in London from June 19 to 27, 2027, bringing together artists and cultural institutions from India and the UK for a multidisciplinary programme across South Kensington.Titled Serendipity Arts Festival London, the event will be presented in partnership with the Great Exhibition Road Festival, led by Imperial College London, and several cultural institutions in the area. These include the Science Museum, V&A South Kensington, Natural History Museum, Royal Albert Hall, Royal Geographical Society, Royal College of Music and Royal College of Art.The festival aims to create a platform for artistic exchange between India, the UK and the wider world, extending the organisation’s work beyond its annual festival in Goa. Its programme will span new media, visual arts, dance, music and culinary arts, with an all-women, intergenerational curatorial team.The curatorial team includes Veeranganakumari Solanki and Nancy Adajania for new media, Latika Gupta for visual arts, Preethi Athreya for dance, Sneha Khanwalkar for music and Elizabeth Yorke for culinary arts.The London edition will also be linked to the 11th Serendipity Arts Festival, scheduled to take place in Panjim, Goa, from December 13 to 20, 2026. As part of this exchange, UK institutions and cultural partners, including the Natural History Museum, Royal Geographical Society, British Film Institute and Royal College of Art, will present projects at the Goa festival.The London event will be held along Exhibition Road and across the South Kensington Cultural Quarter from June 19 to 27, 2027.
